historical_importance: A major composer of the 1970s–2000s and the composer of most of his brother Rakesh Roshan's films.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for all four films Khan made with Rakesh Roshan: King Uncle, Karan Arjun, Koyla and Krazzy 4.
biography: Rajesh Roshan, born Rajesh Roshanlal Nagrath on 24 May 1955 in Bombay, is the son of the composer Roshan and the singer Ira Roshan, the younger brother of the filmmaker Rakesh Roshan and the uncle of Hrithik Roshan. He shot to fame with Kunwara Baap (1974) and Julie (1975), which won him the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director, and worked frequently with Kishore Kumar, Basu Chatterjee and Dev Anand on films such as Des Pardes, Man Pasand and Lootmaar. He later won Filmfare Awards for his brother's films, including Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai. He composed the songs for all four of Rakesh Roshan's projects with Shah Rukh Khan: King Uncle (1993), Karan Arjun (1995), which earned him a Filmfare nomination, Koyla (1997) and Krazzy 4 (2008), in which Khan appears in a song.

name: Rakesh Roshan
function: Director; producer; screenwriter (Filmkraft Productions); former actor
career_background: Appeared in 84 films as an actor in the 1970s and 1980s, mostly in supporting roles, before becoming a director and producer; son of the composer Roshan and brother of Rajesh Roshan.
debut: Khudgarz (1987) began a run of directorial successes with titles beginning with 'K'.
major_works: Khudgarz (1987); Khoon Bhari Maang (1988); Kishen Kanhaiya (1990); King Uncle (1993); Karan Arjun (1995); Koyla (1997); Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai (2000); Koi... Mil Gaya (2003); the Krrish series (2006–2013)
recurring_themes: Revenge dramas, reincarnation and family melodrama; later science fiction and superheroes.
creative_style: Large-scale commercial entertainment built on family bonds and retribution.
major_awards: Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director for Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai and Koi... Mil Gaya
historical_importance: A leading commercial director-producer whose 'K' films span three decades; King Uncle gave Khan one of his early successful supporting roles.
relationship_with_actor: Directed and produced three films with Khan and produced a fourth, in which Khan appears in a song; King Uncle was their first film together.
biography: Rakesh Roshan Nagrath, born on 6 September 1949, is the son of the composer Roshan and the brother of the composer Rajesh Roshan. He appeared in 84 films in the 1970s and 1980s, mainly in supporting roles in big-budget productions, before building a second career as a producer and director. From Khudgarz (1987) onwards he became known for successes with titles beginning with the letter 'K', among them Khoon Bhari Maang (1988), Kishen Kanhaiya (1990), Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai (2000) and Koi... Mil Gaya (2003); the last two won him the Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director. His first film with Shah Rukh Khan was the family comedy King Uncle (1993), one of the few early successes in which Khan played a second lead. Roshan then made Karan Arjun (1995), a reincarnation-revenge saga pairing Khan with Salman Khan that became the second-highest-grossing film of the year, and Koyla (1997), with Khan as a mute servant who rebels against a tyrant. He also produced and wrote the story for Krazzy 4 (2008), in which Khan appears in a song. His later work includes the Krrish superhero series with his son Hrithik Roshan, and the Roshan family was the subject of the 2025 Netflix documentary The Roshans.

name: Ritesh Sidhwani
career_background: A Mumbai-born Hindi-film producer from a Sindhi family who co-founded Excel Entertainment with Farhan Akhtar and has run its business side since its first film.
debut: Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Excel's first production, which won a National Film Award.
major_works: With Khan: Don (2006), Luck by Chance (2009), Don 2 (2011), Raees (2017). Wider work: Dil Chahta Hai, Fukrey, Dil Dhadakne Do, Gully Boy; the streaming series Inside Edge, Mirzapur and Made in Heaven.
recurring_themes: Urban, star-driven genre films alongside smaller writer-led projects; from 2017 a large slate of streaming series.
major_awards: National Film Award for Dil Chahta Hai (as producer); BAFTA for Best Children's & Family Film for Boong (2025).
historical_importance: One of the producers who moved Excel from a single hit into a durable studio and an early leader in Indian streaming content.
relationship_with_actor: Four films, all Excel productions: the two Don films that rebuilt Khan as an action lead in his forties, Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance with Khan as himself, and Rahul Dholakia's Raees, in which Khan played a Gujarat bootlegger. Don and Don 2 are the core of the relationship.
biography: Ritesh Sidhwani co-founded Excel Entertainment with Farhan Akhtar and has produced every Excel film since Dil Chahta Hai (2001), whose National Award established the company. His work with Shah Rukh Khan is concentrated in two Akhtar-directed films: Don (2006), a remake of the 1978 Amitabh Bachchan thriller that was a hit in India and a blockbuster overseas, and its sequel Don 2 (2011), which was shot partly in Berlin. Between them came Luck by Chance (2009), Zoya Akhtar's satire of the Hindi film industry, in which Khan appears as himself. Raees (2017), a Gujarat crime drama, was a moderate success. Excel later became one of the most active producers of Indian streaming series, including Inside Edge, Mirzapur and Made in Heaven, and Sidhwani won a BAFTA in 2025 for producing Boong.

name: Yash Johar
career_background: Born in Amritsar; began in the early 1950s as a publicist and still photographer at Filmistan, then handled production for Sunil Dutt's Ajanta Arts and Dev Anand's Navketan Films.
debut: Founded Dharma Productions in 1976; first production Dostana (1980).
major_works: Guide (1965, production); Jewel Thief (1967, production); Dostana (1980); Agneepath (1990); Duplicate (1998); Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998); Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001); Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003)
recurring_themes: Indian traditions and family values; lavish sets and exotic locations.
major_awards: Kuch Kuch Hota Hai won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment.
historical_importance: Founder of Dharma Productions and a respected production controller on classic Navketan films; father of Karan Johar.
relationship_with_actor: Credited producer of four Khan films, including his son Karan Johar's first two features, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham.
biography: Yash Johar (6 September 1929 – 26 June 2004) was born in Amritsar and began his film career in the early 1950s as a publicist and still photographer at Sashadhar Mukherjee's Filmistan studio. He was a production executive on Love in Simla (1960), joined Sunil Dutt's Ajanta Arts in 1962, and became known as a skilled production controller with Dev Anand's Navketan Films on Guide (1965), Jewel Thief (1967), Prem Pujari (1970) and Hare Rama Hare Krishna (1971). He married Hiroo Johar, Yash Chopra's sister, in 1971; their son Karan was born in 1972. In 1976 he founded Dharma Productions, whose films became known for lavish sets, exotic locations and an emphasis on Indian traditions and family values. He produced Shah Rukh Khan's Duplicate (1998) and then Karan Johar's Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998), a turning point that won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film. He went on to produce Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) and Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), both starring Khan. He died in Mumbai in June 2004 of a chest infection while also battling cancer.

name: Akash Khurana
career_background: An actor, screenwriter, director, author and theatre artist trained as a mechanical engineer (NIT Rourkela) with an MBA from XLRI and a doctorate from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, where he has taught since 1995.
debut: First screen appearance in Shyam Benegal's Kalyug (1981); as a writer, Aashiqui (1990).
major_works: With Khan: Baazigar (1993), Chaahat (1996), Duplicate (1998). As writer, over 20 screenplays including Aashiqui and Baazigar; as actor, nearly 60 films including Ardh Satya, Saaransh, Sarfarosh, Company and Barfi!.
recurring_themes: Screenplays for early-1990s romantic thrillers and melodramas, much of it for Mahesh Bhatt.
major_awards: Nandi Award (Special Jury) for Dr. Ambedkar (1992).
historical_importance: A writer behind two of the defining early-1990s Hindi hits, Aashiqui and Baazigar.
relationship_with_actor: Three screenplays for Khan in five years. Baazigar (1993) gave him his breakthrough as an anti-hero lead; Chaahat (1996) and Duplicate (1998), both directed by Mahesh Bhatt, did poorly.
biography: Akash Khurana has had parallel careers as an actor, a screenwriter and an academic. After engineering and management degrees he made his first screen appearance in Shyam Benegal's Kalyug and went on to act in nearly sixty films, from Ardh Satya and Saaransh to Company and Barfi!. As a writer he is credited with more than twenty screenplays, including Aashiqui and Baazigar. Baazigar (1993), Abbas–Mustan's thriller in which Khan plays a revenge-driven murderer who romances the daughters of the man he blames for his family's ruin, was a major commercial success and made Khan's anti-hero image. Khurana's other two Khan credits, Mahesh Bhatt's Chaahat (1996) and Duplicate (1998), were below average and a failure respectively. He has been visiting faculty at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences since 1995.

name: Anand–Milind
career_background: Brothers Anand and Milind Srivastava, sons of the composer Chitragupt.
debut: Ab Ayega Mazaa (1984); breakthrough with Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988).
major_works: Ab Ayega Mazaa (1984); Jalwa (1987); Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988); Baaghi (1990); Dil Aashna Hai (1992); Anjaam (1994); Army (1996)
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Music Director (Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak)
historical_importance: Composed for over 200 Bollywood films.
relationship_with_actor: Scored three early Khan films: Dil Aashna Hai, Anjaam and Army.
biography: Anand–Milind are the composer brothers Anand and Milind Srivastava, sons of the composer Chitragupt, who have written music for over 200 Bollywood films. They debuted in 1984 with Ab Ayega Mazaa and scored Jalwa (1987) before their breakthrough with the romantic musical Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), which won them the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director; Baaghi (1990) followed. They composed the songs for three of Shah Rukh Khan's early films: Hema Malini's Dil Aashna Hai (1992), Rahul Rawail's thriller Anjaam (1994), with lyrics by Sameer, and the action film Army (1996), in which Khan makes a special appearance.

name: Champak Jain
career_background: A Hindi-film producer and co-owner of Venus Records & Tapes, the music and video company he ran with his brothers and which became one of the major Hindi-film producers of the 1990s.
debut: Khiladi (1992), the first Venus production.
major_works: With Khan: Baazigar (1993), Yes Boss (1997), Josh (2000). Wider work: Khiladi, Main Khiladi Tu Anari, Humraaz, Hulchul.
recurring_themes: Music-led commercial thrillers and romances.
historical_importance: Part of the Jain family that turned a cassette business into a leading 1990s film producer.
relationship_with_actor: Three Venus productions with Khan as lead: Baazigar, his breakthrough; Aziz Mirza's romantic comedy Yes Boss, a hit; and Mansoor Khan's Goa gang musical Josh, an average performer.
biography: Champak Jain was one of the Jain brothers who owned Venus Records & Tapes, a Mumbai cassette and video business that began producing films in the early 1990s and quickly became one of the main sources of commercial Hindi cinema. Venus productions credited to him include Khiladi (1992), Main Khiladi Tu Anari (1994), Humraaz (2002) and Hulchul (2004). For Shah Rukh Khan the company's significance rests on Baazigar (1993), the Abbas–Mustan thriller that made him a star by casting him as a murderer; Venus also backed Yes Boss (1997), a romantic comedy and hit, and Josh (2000), a musical set among Goa gangs. Jain died on 31 October 2019, aged 52.

name: Dreamz Unlimited
function: Production company founded by Shah Rukh Khan, Juhi Chawla and Aziz Mirza
career_background: Set up in 1999 as a partnership of Khan, Juhi Chawla and Aziz Mirza; after it dissolved, Khan and Gauri Khan restructured it as Red Chillies Entertainment.
debut: First production: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000).
major_works: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000); Aśoka (2001); Chalte Chalte (2003); distribution of the Hindi version of Hey Ram (2000)
major_awards: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani won the IIFA Award for Best Special Effects; Aśoka won Filmfare and IIFA awards for Best Cinematography.
historical_importance: Khan's first venture as a producer and the forerunner of Red Chillies Entertainment.
relationship_with_actor: Khan's own first production company; it produced three films starring him and distributed Hey Ram, in which he co-starred.
biography: Dreamz Unlimited was founded in 1999 by Shah Rukh Khan, Juhi Chawla and Aziz Mirza, marking Khan's move into production. Its first film, Mirza's media satire Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), starring Khan and Chawla, was a commercial failure that Khan later called the biggest failure for all three partners, though it won the IIFA Award for Best Special Effects. The company also distributed the Hindi version of Kamal Haasan's Hey Ram (2000), in which Khan co-starred. It produced Santosh Sivan's historical epic Aśoka (2001), acclaimed abroad but only moderately successful in India. Mirza's Chalte Chalte (2003) was the company's first box-office hit and its last production before it became Red Chillies Entertainment. Khan's article says that after the partnership dissolved, Khan and Gauri Khan restructured the company as Red Chillies. The sources differ on dates: the Red Chillies article gives its founding as 2002, while the Chalte Chalte article places the rebranding in 2003.

name: Farah Khan
career_background: One of Hindi cinema's leading choreographers, with more than a hundred songs in over 80 films, before directing.
debut: Directorial debut Main Hoon Na (2004), produced by Red Chillies Entertainment.
major_works: Main Hoon Na (2004); Om Shanti Om (2007); Tees Maar Khan (2010); Happy New Year (2014); choreography for Monsoon Wedding and Bombay Dreams
recurring_themes: Affectionate homage to Hindi popular cinema, masala spectacle and self-referential comedy.
creative_style: Retro, song-and-dance-driven entertainment that plays with Bollywood clichés.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Choreography; seven Filmfare Awards for Best Choreography, including 'Chaiyya Chaiyya' (Dil Se..); Filmfare Best Director nominations for Main Hoon Na and Om Shanti Om; Tony Award and Golden Horse nominations for choreography
historical_importance: A rare woman director of big-budget masala hits, whose films with Khan were among the top earners of their years.
relationship_with_actor: A close friend since the sets of Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa; she choreographed 'Chaiyya Chaiyya' in Dil Se.. and directed Khan in three of her four features, all Red Chillies productions: Main Hoon Na, Om Shanti Om and Happy New Year.
biography: Farah Khan, born on 9 January 1965, is a film director, choreographer, writer and producer who has choreographed more than a hundred songs in over 80 films. She has won the National Film Award for Best Choreography and seven Filmfare Awards, and her work on Bombay Dreams and elsewhere brought Tony and Golden Horse nominations. She met Shah Rukh Khan on the sets of Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa (1994), and the two became close friends and regular collaborators; her choreography for 'Chaiyya Chaiyya' in Dil Se.. (1998) won a Filmfare Award. She made her directorial debut with Main Hoon Na (2004), a masala film produced by Red Chillies Entertainment in which Khan plays an army major undercover at a college; it was the second highest-grossing Indian film of the year. She followed it with the reincarnation melodrama Om Shanti Om (2007), which introduced Deepika Padukone opposite Khan and paid tribute to 1970s Hindi cinema. Both films earned her Filmfare Best Director nominations. After Tees Maar Khan (2010) she directed Khan again in the heist musical Happy New Year (2014), which set a record opening day but drew mixed reviews.

name: Ganesh Jain
career_background: A Hindi-film producer who, with his brothers Ratan, Girish, Champak, Umed, Ramesh and Bhawar Jain, founded Venus Records & Tapes; he has served as chairman of the Indian Music Industry body.
debut: Venus began as a video-cassette manufacturer in the early 1980s and moved into film production in 1992 with Khiladi.
major_works: With Khan: Baazigar (1993), Baadshah (1999), Josh (2000). Wider work: Garam Masala, Aap Ki Khatir, De Dana Dan.
recurring_themes: Song-driven mainstream entertainers, from thrillers to comedies.
historical_importance: Co-founder of one of the largest music-rights holders and film producers of 1990s Bollywood.
relationship_with_actor: Three films with Khan as lead, all Venus productions: Baazigar, Abbas–Mustan's spy comedy Baadshah, and Josh.
biography: Ganesh Jain and his brother Ratan built Venus Records & Tapes from a video-cassette manufacturing business in the early 1980s into a film producer from 1992, beginning with Khiladi. Over the following two decades the company acquired a large library of audio, satellite, video and cable rights, and Jain was elected chairman of the Indian Music Industry. Venus was the producer of Baazigar (1993), the thriller that established Shah Rukh Khan as a leading man, and returned to Khan and the Abbas–Mustan directing team with Baadshah (1999), a comic spy caper that performed averagely. Josh (2000) cast Khan as a Goa gang leader opposite Aishwarya Rai, who played his twin sister. Later Venus productions include Garam Masala, Aap Ki Khatir and De Dana Dan.

name: Juhi Chawla
career_background: An Indian actress, Miss India 1984, who was one of the leading heroines of Hindi cinema from the late 1980s to the early 2000s and later moved to art-house roles.
debut: Sultanat (1986); breakthrough in Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), opposite Aamir Khan, which won her the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut.
major_works: With Khan as producer: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), Aśoka (2001), Chalte Chalte (2003). As actress: Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Darr, Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke, Yes Boss, Jhankaar Beats, My Brother Nikhil, I Am.
recurring_themes: Comic romantic heroines in the 1990s; independent and character roles from the 2000s.
major_awards: Two Filmfare Awards, including Best Actress for Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993).
historical_importance: One of the most popular Hindi-film heroines of the 1990s, and Khan's most frequent leading lady of that decade.
relationship_with_actor: Khan and Chawla co-founded Dreamz Unlimited, which produced three films, starting with the self-starring Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), a flop; Santosh Sivan's Aśoka (2001) followed, then Aziz Mirza's Chalte Chalte (2003), a hit. She is also co-owner, with her husband Jay Mehta and Khan, of the Kolkata Knight Riders. Her on-screen pairings with Khan are recorded in Romances.
biography: Juhi Chawla won Miss India in 1984 and became one of Hindi cinema's leading actresses after Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), which earned her the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut. She won Best Actress for Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke in 1993, a year that also produced Darr with Shah Rukh Khan, and from the 2000s took art-house roles in Jhankaar Beats, 3 Deewarein, My Brother Nikhil and I Am. Her producing work is almost entirely with Khan. The two founded Dreamz Unlimited, whose first film, Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), starred them both as rival television reporters and failed commercially. The company then backed Aśoka (2001) and Chalte Chalte (2003), the last of which was a hit. Their partnership continued off screen as co-owners of the Kolkata Knight Riders cricket team.

name: Mahesh Bhatt
career_background: Son of the director Nanabhai Bhatt; turned producer in 1987 with his brother Mukesh Bhatt under the Vishesh Films banner.
debut: Saaransh (1984) was India's official Academy Award entry; Naam (1986) was his first commercial film.
major_works: Saaransh (1984); Naam (1986); Daddy (1989); Aashiqui (1990); Dil Hai Ki Manta Nahin (1991); Sadak (1991); Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993); Chaahat (1996); Tamanna (1996); Duplicate (1998)
recurring_themes: Unconventional narratives and bold themes, alongside commercial romances.
creative_style: Moves between art-house films and mainstream romantic hits.
major_awards: 5 National Film Awards, including the Special Jury Award for Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke; 4 Filmfare Awards
historical_importance: One of the most prominent Hindi filmmakers of the 1980s and 1990s, known for mentoring and launching actors; inducted into the Bollywood Walk of Fame in 2013.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan in the romantic thriller Chaahat and the double-role comedy Duplicate, and produced Gudgudee, in which Khan appears as himself.
biography: Mahesh Bhatt, born on 20 September 1948, is the son of the director Nanabhai Bhatt and a retired director, producer and screenwriter known for unconventional narratives and bold themes. His early Saaransh (1984) was India's official entry for the Academy Awards, and Naam (1986) was his first commercial success. In 1987 he became a producer with his younger brother Mukesh Bhatt under Vishesh Films. He moved between art-house work such as Daddy (1989) and Swayam (1991) and romantic hits such as Aashiqui (1990), Dil Hai Ki Manta Nahin (1991) and Sadak (1991). He won five National Film Awards, including the Special Jury Award for directing Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993) and the award for Tamanna (1996), and four Filmfare Awards. With Shah Rukh Khan, Bhatt directed Chaahat (1996), in which Khan's singer is persecuted by an obsessive heiress, and produced Basu Chatterjee's Gudgudee (1997), in which Khan appears as himself. He also directed Duplicate (1998), Khan's first film with Dharma Productions, in which Khan plays both a gentle chef and his gangster double. His half-brother Robin Bhatt co-wrote both Chaahat and Duplicate. Bhatt was inducted into the Bollywood Walk of Fame in 2013.

name: Manoj Lalwani
career_background: A writer credited on 3 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000) and One 2 Ka 4 (2001).
relationship_with_actor: 3 films with Khan, credited as writer: Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), directed by Aziz Mirza, with Khan in the lead as Raj "Raju" Mathur; verdict: Commercial success. Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), directed by Aziz Mirza, with Khan in the lead as Ajay Bakshi; verdict: Flop. One 2 Ka 4 (2001), directed by Shashilal K. Nair, with Khan in the lead as ACP Arun Verma; verdict: Disaster.
biography: Manoj Lalwani is credited as writer on Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000) and One 2 Ka 4 (2001). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Mushtaq Shiekh
career_background: A Mumbai-born screenwriter, author, producer and actor, and the author of the Shah Rukh Khan biography Still Reading Khan.
debut: Om Shanti Om (2007), co-written for Farah Khan.
major_works: With Khan: Om Shanti Om (2007), Billu (2009), Ra.One (2011). Wider work: Rangrezz; Ek Deewane Ki Deewaniyat (2025); the novel Secrets Within (2024).
recurring_themes: Big commercial star vehicles; books about Hindi cinema.
historical_importance: A writer closely tied to Khan's Red Chillies output of the late 2000s and one of his biographers.
relationship_with_actor: Three screenplays for Khan in four years: Om Shanti Om, a reincarnation melodrama and tribute to 1970s Hindi cinema; Priyadarshan's Billu, a Red Chillies production in which Khan plays a film star; and Ra.One, Khan's superhero film. He also wrote Khan's biography, Still Reading Khan.
biography: Mushtaq Shiekh is a screenwriter and author whose film career is closely linked to Shah Rukh Khan. He co-wrote Om Shanti Om (2007), Farah Khan's reincarnation drama and celebration of 1970s Hindi film, in which Khan plays a junior artist reborn as a star; Billu (2009), Priyadarshan's remake of a Malayalam film about a barber whose childhood friend is now a superstar, played by Khan; and Ra.One (2011), Khan's expensive superhero film. He also wrote Still Reading Khan, a biography of the actor, and several other books about Hindi cinema. Away from Khan he wrote Priyadarshan's Rangrezz, worked as associate producer on Mulk (2018) and as a creative director at Sahara One, and wrote the 2025 romance Ek Deewane Ki Deewaniyat.

name: Neeraj Vora
career_background: A Gujarati writer, director, actor and composer, born in Bhuj and raised in Mumbai, the son of the classical musician Vinayak Rai Vora; he began in Gujarati theatre and television.
debut: Worked on Ketan Mehta's Holi (1984); made his mark as a writer on Ram Gopal Varma's Rangeela (1995); directorial debut Khiladi 420 (2000).
major_works: With Khan: Pehla Nasha (1993), Baadshah (1999), Josh (2000). Wider work: Hera Pheri (writer), Phir Hera Pheri (director), Garam Masala, Bhagam Bhag, Golmaal, Bhool Bhulaiyaa (writer).
recurring_themes: Mass comedy dialogue and screenplays, especially for Priyadarshan.
historical_importance: One of the main comedy writers of 2000s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Three credits on Khan films, none central: Pehla Nasha, in which Khan appears as himself and for which Vora is credited with both writing and songs; Abbas–Mustan's spy comedy Baadshah; and Mansoor Khan's Josh, both as writer. None was more than an average performer.
biography: Neeraj Vora came from a family of musicians in Gujarat and began as a stage and television actor before turning to film writing. He made his mark with Rangeela (1995), even playing a role in it when an actor was absent, and became one of the main comedy writers of the 2000s, with credits on the Hera Pheri films, Garam Masala, Bhagam Bhag, Golmaal and Bhool Bhulaiyaa. He directed Khiladi 420 and Phir Hera Pheri. His connection to Shah Rukh Khan is peripheral: he wrote and composed songs for Ashutosh Gowariker's Pehla Nasha, in which Khan appears as himself, and wrote for Baadshah (1999) and Josh (2000), both averages. Vora suffered a stroke in October 2016 while preparing Hera Pheri 3 and died on 14 December 2017.

name: Nikhil–Vinay
career_background: Nikhil Kamath and Vinay Tiwari, both classically trained, were discovered by the singer Anuradha Paudwal and recommended to Gulshan Kumar of T-Series.
debut: Pyar Bhara Dil (1991).
major_works: Pyar Bhara Dil (1991); Bewafa Sanam (1995); English Babu Desi Mem (1996); Tum Bin (2001); Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002); Yeh Lamhe Judaai Ke (2004)
recurring_themes: Sentimental romantic songs, mostly for T-Series.
historical_importance: Bewafa Sanam was a breakthrough for the singer Sonu Nigam; they also composed his albums Jaan and Yaad.
relationship_with_actor: Composed for three Khan films: English Babu Desi Mem, Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam and the long-delayed Yeh Lamhe Judaai Ke.
biography: Nikhil–Vinay were the composer duo of Nikhil Kamath and Vinay Tiwari, active in Hindi films from 1991 until they split in 2006. Both classically trained, they were discovered by Anuradha Paudwal, who recommended them to T-Series owner Gulshan Kumar and the director Chandra Barot, who signed them for Pyar Bhara Dil (1991). Their early successes included Bewafa Sanam (1995), which launched Sonu Nigam as a playback singer, English Babu Desi Mem (1996), Uff Yeh Mohabbat (1997) and Papa The Great (2000), and they composed Nigam's albums Jaan and Yaad. Their later hits included Tum Bin (2001) and Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002). They composed for three Shah Rukh Khan films: English Babu Desi Mem, Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam and Yeh Lamhe Judaai Ke (2004).

name: Ratan Jain
career_background: A producer credited on 3 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: Yes Boss (1997), Josh (2000) and Main Hoon Na (2004).
relationship_with_actor: 3 films with Khan, credited as producer: Yes Boss (1997), directed by Aziz Mirza, with Khan in the lead as Rahul Joshi; verdict: Hit. Josh (2000), directed by Mansoor Khan, with Khan in the lead as Max Dias; verdict: Average. Main Hoon Na (2004), directed by Farah Khan, with Khan in the lead as Major Ram Prasad Sharma; verdict: Commercial success.
biography: Ratan Jain is credited as producer on Yes Boss (1997), Josh (2000) and Main Hoon Na (2004). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Ravi Kapoor
career_background: A writer credited on 3 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: King Uncle (1993), Karan Arjun (1995) and Koyla (1997).
relationship_with_actor: 3 films with Khan, credited as writer: King Uncle (1993), directed by Rakesh Roshan, with Khan in a supporting role as Anil Bansal; verdict: Moderate box-office success. Karan Arjun (1995), directed by Rakesh Roshan, with Khan in a co-lead as Arjun Singh; verdict: All-time blockbuster. Koyla (1997), directed by Rakesh Roshan, with Khan in the lead as Shankar Thakur; verdict: Average.
biography: Ravi Kapoor is credited as writer on King Uncle (1993), Karan Arjun (1995) and Koyla (1997). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Sachin Bhowmick
career_background: A Bengali-born Hindi-film writer who wrote stories or screenplays for over 94 films across five decades and contributed to the Bengali film magazine Ultorath.
debut: Screenplay of Mohan Segal's Lajwanti (1958).
major_works: With Khan: Karan Arjun (1995), Koyla (1997), Achanak (1998). Wider work: Anuradha, An Evening in Paris, Brahmachari, Aradhana, Gol Maal, Karz, Karma, Koi Mil Gaya, Krrish; directed Raja Rani (1973).
recurring_themes: Romance, comedy and reincarnation or revenge melodrama across the mainstream.
historical_importance: One of the longest-serving writers in Hindi cinema, with hits in every decade from the 1960s to the 2000s.
relationship_with_actor: Three films, two of them for Rakesh Roshan: the reincarnation revenge epic Karan Arjun (1995), an all-time blockbuster with Khan and Salman Khan as reborn brothers, and the action romance Koyla (1997). Achanak (1998), in which Khan appears as himself, failed.
biography: Sachin Bhowmick wrote for Hindi cinema for half a century, from Lajwanti (1958) to Krrish (2006), and is credited with stories or screenplays for more than ninety films. His successes include Anuradha, An Evening in Paris, Brahmachari, Aradhana, Gol Maal, Karz and Karma; he directed one film, Raja Rani (1973). In the 1990s he worked chiefly with Rakesh Roshan, for whom he wrote Karan Arjun (1995), the reincarnation revenge story in which Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan play murdered brothers reborn to avenge their mother, and Koyla (1997), with Khan as a mute servant fighting a feudal tyrant. Karan Arjun was one of the biggest hits of the decade. Bhowmick continued with Roshan into Koi Mil Gaya and Krrish. He died on 12 April 2011.

name: Sandeep Chowta
career_background: Born in Ghana, raised in Nigeria and Bangalore; son of the Tulu author D. K. Chowta; head of Columbia Records in India and a core member of the group AO Music.
major_works: Aśoka (2001, score); Om Shanti Om (2007, score); Billu (2009, score); 12 Telugu films
historical_importance: AO Music albums crediting him have charted in the international top five.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Aśoka, Om Shanti Om and Billu.
biography: Sandeep Chowta, born in 1967 or 1968 in Ghana, grew up in Nigeria before moving to Bangalore; he is the son of D. K. Chowta, a Tulu author and businessman. He works mainly in Hindi and Telugu cinema, has composed music for 12 Telugu films, and heads Columbia Records in India. In 2003 he produced the anti-substance-abuse documentary Dead End, and since 2004 he has been a core member of the new-age group AO Music, whose albums have charted in the international top five. For Shah Rukh Khan he wrote the background scores of Santosh Sivan's Aśoka (2001), Farah Khan's Om Shanti Om (2007) and Priyadarshan's Billu (2009), while other composers wrote their songs.

name: Sanjay Chhel
career_background: A Gujarati-born writer, lyricist and director, son of the art director Chhel Vayeda, who started in Gujarati theatre and wrote more than 30 television serials, including Nukkad.
debut: Pehla Nasha (1993) as writer; Khoobsurat (1999) as director.
major_works: With Khan: Pehla Nasha (1993), Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), Kismat Konnection (2008). Wider work: Kachche Dhaage, Partner, Dil Toh Baccha Hai Ji (dialogue and lyrics); directed Kyaa Dil Ne Kahaa and Maan Gaye Mughal-e-Azam.
recurring_themes: Light comedy and romance; Gujarati columns and fiction.
relationship_with_actor: Three peripheral credits: Pehla Nasha, with Khan as himself; Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, Khan's first Dreamz Unlimited production, a flop; and Kismat Konnection, which Khan narrates.
biography: Sanjay Chhel grew up in Mumbai as the son of the production designer Chhel Vayeda and began writing one-act plays in Gujarati before moving into television, where he wrote more than thirty serials. His film debut as a writer was Pehla Nasha (1993), which includes a cameo by Shah Rukh Khan as himself, and he went on to write the stories of Kachche Dhaage, Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, Partner and Kismat Konnection. Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), a media satire starring Khan and Juhi Chawla, was the first production of their company Dreamz Unlimited and failed at the box office; Kismat Konnection (2008) uses Khan as narrator. Chhel has also directed Khoobsurat, Kyaa Dil Ne Kahaa and Maan Gaye Mughal-e-Azam and writes weekly columns for Gujarati dailies.

name: Surinder Sodhi
career_background: Often credited as Surender or Surendra Sodhi.
major_works: Deewana (1992); Soldier (1998); Raja Hindustani (1996); Baadshah (1999); Hera Pheri (2000); 23rd March 1931: Shaheed (2002); Special 26 (2013)
relationship_with_actor: Scored Baadshah, Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega and Shaurya; his article also credits him with the background score of Khan's debut, Deewana.
biography: Surinder Sodhi, often credited as Surender or Surendra Sodhi, is an Indian film-score composer whose short Wikipedia article lists background scores for Deewana, Soldier, Raja Hindustani, Baadshah, Hera Pheri, 23rd March 1931: Shaheed and Special 26. For Shah Rukh Khan's films, the film articles credit him with the background scores of Abbas–Mustan's Baadshah (1999), Raj Kanwar's Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000) and Samar Khan's Shaurya (2008). The Deewana credit comes only from his own article; the Deewana film article does not name a score composer.

name: Abbas Tyrewala
career_background: A Mumbai-born screenwriter, lyricist and director who first worked as a lyricist and became known as a dialogue writer in the early 2000s.
debut: Dialogue for Aśoka (2001); directorial debut Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na (2008).
major_works: With Khan: Aśoka (2001), Main Hoon Na (2004). Wider work: Maqbool, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S., Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na, Jhootha Hi Sahi; dialogue for Pathaan (2023).
recurring_themes: Sharp, colloquial dialogue for both prestige and mainstream films.
historical_importance: A key dialogue writer of 2000s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Two dialogue credits on Khan films: Santosh Sivan's historical epic Aśoka, a Dreamz Unlimited production, and Farah Khan's Main Hoon Na, a commercial success. He later wrote Pathaan's dialogue, which falls outside these two credited films.
biography: Abbas Tyrewala began as a lyricist on Dil Pe Mat Le Yaar!! and Love Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega and moved into dialogue writing with Aśoka (2001), Santosh Sivan's film about the Mauryan emperor starring Shah Rukh Khan. He wrote for Maqbool and Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. in 2003 and for Farah Khan's Main Hoon Na (2004), a Red Chillies action comedy in which Khan plays an army officer posing as a college student. As director he made Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na (2008), a hit romantic comedy with an A. R. Rahman soundtrack, and Jhootha Hi Sahi (2010). His later work with Khan includes the dialogue for Pathaan (2023).

name: Abbas–Mustan
career_background: Brothers Abbas and Mustan Burmawalla began as film editors with their brother Hussain and worked as assistant directors to Govindbhai Patel.
debut: The Gujarati film Sajan Tara Sambharana (1985); their first Hindi film was Agneekaal (1990).
major_works: Sajan Tara Sambharana (1985); Agneekaal (1990); Baazigar (1993); Baadshah (1999)
recurring_themes: Suspense, action and romantic thrillers with dark themes.
creative_style: Stylish, twist-driven thrillers.
major_awards: Life Membership of the International Film and Television Club, Asian Academy of Film & Television
historical_importance: Their Baazigar broke with the Bollywood formula by making the hero a murderer, a turning point in Khan's early career.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan as the murderous avenger in Baazigar, which won him the Filmfare Award for Best Actor, and as the bumbling detective in the comedy thriller Baadshah.
biography: Abbas–Mustan are the brothers Abbas Alibhai Burmawalla and Mustan Alibhai Burmawalla. With their brother Hussain they began as film editors and then worked as assistant directors to Govindbhai Patel. When Patel turned down the chance to direct the Gujarati film Sajan Tara Sambharana (1985), the brothers took the job and launched their directing career. Their first Hindi film was Agneekaal (1990), and they have since directed more than fourteen Hindi films, becoming known for stylish suspense, action and romantic thrillers with dark themes. They later founded the production house Burmawalla Partners. Their second film with Shah Rukh Khan was the comedy thriller Baadshah (1999), in which he plays a bumbling detective mistaken for a secret agent. The first, Baazigar (1993), loosely based on A Kiss Before Dying, cast him as an avenger who kills his girlfriend; Khan's article describes it as an unexpected violation of the standard Bollywood formula. It was a major commercial success and won Khan the Filmfare Award for Best Actor.

name: Amar Mohile
career_background: Son of the composer Anil Mohile.
major_works: Chennai Express (2013, score); Dilwale (2015, score)
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Rohit Shetty's two Khan films, Chennai Express and Dilwale.
biography: Amar Mohile is an Indian film-score composer working mainly in Hindi films and the son of the composer Anil Mohile. His Wikipedia article gives little biographical detail beyond a discography. In Shah Rukh Khan's films he is credited with the background scores of Rohit Shetty's action comedies Chennai Express (2013), whose songs were by Vishal–Shekhar, and Dilwale (2015), whose songs were by Pritam.

name: Amit Trivedi
career_background: Composed for theatre, advertising jingles and independent music before films.
debut: Aamir (2008).
major_works: Aamir (2008); Dev.D (2009); Bombay Talkies (2013); Udta Punjab (2016); Dear Zindagi (2016); Secret Superstar (2017); Manmarziyaan (2018)
recurring_themes: Indie-pop sensibility in film music.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction; Filmfare R. D. Burman Award and Best Background Score (55th Filmfare Awards)
historical_importance: A leading independent-minded film composer since the late 2000s.
relationship_with_actor: Composed Bombay Talkies, whose closing song features Khan, and Dear Zindagi.
biography: Amit Trivedi, born on 8 April 1979 in Mumbai, is a composer, singer and lyricist who began with theatre productions, advertising jingles and independent music before his film debut, Aamir (2008). He won the Filmfare R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent and the Filmfare Award for Best Background Score at the 55th Filmfare Awards, along with a National Film Award for Best Music Direction, and later earned consecutive Filmfare nominations for Udta Punjab (2016), Secret Superstar (2017) and Manmarziyaan (2018). He composed the music for Bombay Talkies (2013), the centenary anthology whose song 'Apna Bombay Talkies' features Shah Rukh Khan among many stars, and for Gauri Shinde's Dear Zindagi (2016), with lyrics mostly by Kausar Munir, in which Khan plays a psychologist.

name: Anees Bazmee
career_background: A Hindi-film writer-director, son of the Urdu poet Abdul Hameed 'Nerang' Bazmee, who started as a child actor and assistant director before turning to screenplays.
debut: Assistant director on Prem Rog (1982); writer on Swarg (1990); directorial debut Hulchul (1995).
major_works: With Khan: King Uncle (1993), Army (1996). Wider work as director: Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha, No Entry, Welcome, Singh Is Kinng, Ready, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and 3.
recurring_themes: Broad ensemble comedies and family entertainers.
historical_importance: One of the most commercially successful comedy directors of 2000s–2020s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Two early writing credits: Rakesh Roshan's King Uncle, with Khan in a supporting role, and Army, in which Khan makes an extended special appearance. Both predate Bazmee's directing career.
biography: Anees Bazmee began as a child actor, assisted Raj Kapoor on Prem Rog (1982) and became a screenwriter with David Dhawan's Swarg (1990). In that period he wrote King Uncle (1993), Rakesh Roshan's family comedy with Shah Rukh Khan as the young man who wins over Jackie Shroff's miserly uncle, and Army (1996), in which Khan has an extended special appearance. Bazmee's directing career started with Hulchul (1995) and found commercial success with Pyaar To Hona Hi Tha (1998). He became one of the most reliably profitable comedy directors in Hindi film with No Entry, Welcome, Singh Is Kinng, Ready, Welcome Back and the Bhool Bhulaiyaa sequels. His Khan connection is limited to these early scripts.

name: Anwar Khan
career_background: A writer credited on 2 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: Karan Arjun (1995) and Achanak (1998).
relationship_with_actor: 2 films with Khan, credited as writer: Karan Arjun (1995), directed by Rakesh Roshan, with Khan in a co-lead as Arjun Singh; verdict: All-time blockbuster. Achanak (1998), directed by Naresh Malhotra, with Khan in a self appearance; verdict: Box-office failure.
biography: Anwar Khan is credited as writer on Karan Arjun (1995) and Achanak (1998). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Apoorva Mehta
career_background: A producer credited on 2 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016) and Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022).
relationship_with_actor: 2 films with Khan, credited as producer: Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016), directed by Karan Johar, with Khan in a cameo as Tahir Taliyar Khan. Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022), directed by Ayan Mukerji, with Khan in an extended special appearance as Mohan Bhargav; verdict: Hit (Box Office India).
biography: Apoorva Mehta is credited as producer on Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016) and Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Ashutosh Gowariker
career_background: An actor before turning director; he appeared with Khan in Aziz Mirza's television serial Circus and in the films Chamatkar and Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa.
debut: Directorial debut Pehla Nasha (1993), a thriller remake of Body Double.
major_works: Pehla Nasha (1993); Lagaan (2001); Swades (2004); Jodhaa Akbar (2008); Ventilator (2016, as actor)
recurring_themes: Epic storytelling about community, nationhood and history.
creative_style: Long-form, socially engaged drama, from sport to rural development to period romance.
major_awards: Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director for Lagaan and Jodhaa Akbar; Lagaan was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film.
historical_importance: Lagaan's Academy Award nomination made him a voting member of the Academy; Swades is regarded as a cult classic.
relationship_with_actor: A fellow actor from Khan's television days who later directed him in a cameo in Pehla Nasha and in Swades, one of Khan's most acclaimed performances.
biography: Ashutosh Gowariker, born on 15 February 1964, began as an actor. He appeared alongside Shah Rukh Khan in Aziz Mirza's television serial Circus and played supporting parts in Khan's films Chamatkar (1992) and Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa (1994). He made his directorial debut with Pehla Nasha (1993), a remake of Brian De Palma's Body Double, in which Khan, Aamir Khan and Saif Ali Khan appear as themselves in one scene; the film failed. His breakthrough came with the period sports drama Lagaan (2001), which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and won him the Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director, honours he won again for the historical romance Jodhaa Akbar (2008). Between them came Swades (2004), which he wrote, produced and directed. Khan plays a NASA scientist who returns to an Indian village and builds a micro-hydroelectric plant. The film was a commercial failure but won universal critical acclaim and is now regarded as a cult classic. It earned Khan the Filmfare Award for Best Actor, and Brahmāstra later brought back its hero, Mohan Bhargav. Gowariker returned to acting in Ventilator (2016).

name: B. R. Films
function: Production company founded by B. R. Chopra
career_background: Founded in 1955 by the director B. R. Chopra, a former Lahore film journalist whose youngest brother was Yash Chopra.
major_works: Bhoothnath (2008); Bhoothnath Returns (2014, with T-Series Films)
historical_importance: One of the older Bombay production houses, established after Chopra's success with Afsana (1951).
relationship_with_actor: Produced Bhoothnath, with Khan in an extended special appearance as the father of the boy who befriends a ghost, and co-produced its sequel, in which Khan reprises the role in a cameo.
biography: B. R. Films was formed in 1955 by B. R. Chopra. Born on 22 April 1914 in Rahon, Punjab, and educated at the University of the Punjab in Lahore, Chopra worked as a film journalist with the monthly Cine Herald from 1944 until Partition, when he fled Lahore. His first production, Karwat (1948), flopped, but his directorial debut Afsana (1951), with Ashok Kumar in a double role, was a hit, and he followed it with Chandni Chowk (1954) before founding his own company. His youngest brother was the filmmaker Yash Chopra. For Shah Rukh Khan, B. R. Films, with Ravi Chopra credited as producer, made Vivek Sharma's Bhoothnath (2008), an adaptation of The Canterville Ghost in which Khan plays Aditya Sharma, the father of the boy who befriends a ghost played by Amitabh Bachchan. It was declared a semi-hit. The company co-produced the sequel, Bhoothnath Returns (2014), with T-Series Films, with Renu Ravi Chopra among the producers, and Khan reprised Aditya in a cameo. The Wikipedia page for the company could not be retrieved, so this entry relies on the article about its founder.

name: Bappi Lahiri
career_background: Born Alokesh Aparesh Lahiri; composer and singer who popularised synthesised disco music in Indian film music.
major_works: 1980s–1990s disco-driven film soundtracks; Gudgudee (1997); Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002); World Peace, Love & Harmony (album)
recurring_themes: Disco and synthesised dance music.
major_awards: Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award (63rd Filmfare Awards); Guinness World Record for recording more than 180 songs in one year (1986)
historical_importance: Brought disco into mainstream Indian film music.
relationship_with_actor: Composed Gudgudee, in which Khan appears as himself, and contributed to Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam.
biography: Bappi Lahiri, born Alokesh Aparesh Lahiri (27 November 1952 – 15 February 2022) and known as Bappi Da, was a singer, composer and record producer who popularised synthesised disco in Indian film music. He was especially popular in the 1980s and 1990s, with major box-office successes in Hindi, Telugu and Bengali films, and in 1986 Guinness World Records recognised him for recording more than 180 songs in a year. His album World Peace, Love & Harmony was considered for a Grammy nomination, and he received the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award at the 63rd Filmfare Awards. He composed the music for Basu Chatterjee's comedy Gudgudee (1997), in which Shah Rukh Khan appears as himself, and was among the composers of Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002).

name: Bharat Shah
function: Producer; film financier and distributor (VIP Films)
career_background: Businessman and diamond merchant who works in Hindi films as a financier and distributor under the VIP Films banner.
major_works: Dil Se.. (1998); Devdas (2002); Rascals (2011)
historical_importance: A major financier whose productions include Devdas, the highest-grossing Indian film of 2002.
relationship_with_actor: Co-produced Dil Se.. and produced Devdas, two of Khan's most ambitious tragic romances.
biography: Bharat Shah, born on 5 August 1944, is an Indian businessman, diamond merchant, film financier and distributor who works primarily in Hindi cinema under his banner VIP Films. He was one of the producers of Mani Ratnam's Dil Se.. (1998), with Ratnam, Ram Gopal Varma and Shekhar Kapur, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a journalist in love with a suicide bomber. He produced Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Devdas (2002) under the Mega Bollywood banner, casting Khan as the self-destructive lover opposite Aishwarya Rai and Madhuri Dixit; it became the highest-grossing Indian film of the year and India's Academy Award submission. His later productions include Rascals (2011). His Wikipedia article also includes a section on legal affairs, which this workbook does not cover.

name: Fox Star Studios
function: Production and distribution studio (now Star Studio18)
career_background: Founded in March 2008 as one of 21st Century Fox and Star India's film companies; acquired by Disney in 2019; now a subsidiary of JioStar, renamed Star Studio18 in August 2025.
major_works: My Name Is Khan (2010); Neerja (2016); Chhichhore (2019); The Zoya Factor (2019)
major_awards: National Film Awards for Best Hindi Feature Film for Neerja and Chhichhore
historical_importance: A major studio producing and distributing films in Hindi and other South Asian languages.
relationship_with_actor: Co-produced and distributed My Name Is Khan and produced The Zoya Factor, which Khan narrates.
biography: Star Studio18, formerly Fox Star Studios and then Star Studios, is an Indian motion-picture production and distribution company founded in March 2008 and now wholly owned by JioStar, the joint venture between Reliance and Disney India. It produces Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and other South Asian language films through acquisitions, co-productions and in-house productions. It passed to Disney in March 2019 with 21st Century Fox's film businesses, and adopted its current name in August 2025. Its in-house productions Neerja and Chhichhore won National Film Awards for Best Hindi Feature Film. For Shah Rukh Khan, Fox Star Studios, with Fox Searchlight Pictures, Dharma Productions and Red Chillies Entertainment, backed Karan Johar's My Name Is Khan (2010), which 20th Century Fox released worldwide and which set overseas records for a Hindi film. The studio also produced the sports romance The Zoya Factor (2019), which Khan narrates and which was a box-office disaster.

name: G. P. Sippy
career_background: Born Gopaldas Parmanand Sipahimalani into a wealthy Sindhi trading family; a lawyer who, with his family, fled Sindh as a refugee at Partition and settled in Bombay.
major_works: Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992); Zamaana Deewana (1995)
major_awards: Filmfare Awards in 1968 and 1982
historical_importance: Founder of the Sippy film family and for several years chairman of the Film and TV Producers Guild of India; his grandson is Rohan Sippy.
relationship_with_actor: Produced Aziz Mirza's Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, one of Khan's first lead roles, and Ramesh Sippy's Zamaana Deewana.
biography: G. P. Sippy, born Gopaldas Parmanand Sipahimalani (14 September 1914 – 25 December 2007), was a Bollywood producer and director. He came from a wealthy Sindhi Hindu trading family whose European business contacts shortened the name Sipahimalani to 'Sippy'. A lawyer by training, he was driven from Karachi with his wife Mohini, their children and other relatives as refugees at Partition in 1947, and rebuilt the family's fortunes in Bombay, where they already had trading interests. He chaired the Film and TV Producers Guild of India for several years and won Filmfare Awards in 1968 and 1982. Under Sippy Films he produced two early Shah Rukh Khan films. Aziz Mirza's Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), co-produced by Vivek Vaswani, starred Khan as a small-town engineer in Bombay and won the Filmfare Award for Best Screenplay. Zamaana Deewana (1995), directed by Ramesh Sippy, cast Khan as a gang leader's son and under-performed at the box office.

name: Himesh Reshammiya
debut: Composer debut Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998); acting debut Aap Kaa Surroor (2007).
major_works: Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998); Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005); Silsiilay (2005); 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne'; Aap Kaa Surroor (2007)
recurring_themes: Dance-pop, disco, Sufi-inflected Bollywood songs.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer (2006, 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne'); IIFA and Zee Cine playback awards
historical_importance: Over 1,300 credited songs; ranked 22nd in Bloomberg's list of the world's most influential pop stars in 2025, the only Indian on it.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye and Silsiilay, both 2005 films in which Khan makes brief appearances.
biography: Himesh Reshammiya, born on 23 July 1973, is a playback singer, music director, songwriter, producer and actor with over 1,300 credited songs. He began as a composer with Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998) and later turned to singing; 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne' won him the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine awards for best male playback singer. He made his acting debut in Aap Kaa Surroor (2007). In August 2025 Bloomberg ranked him 22nd among the world's most influential pop stars, the only Indian on the list. In 2005 he composed the songs for two films with brief Shah Rukh Khan appearances: Samar Khan's romantic comedy Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye, where Khan appears as himself, and Khalid Mohamed's Silsiilay, which Khan narrates.

name: Ismail Darbar
career_background: Film-score composer, instrumentalist, singer, violinist and music director.
major_works: Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999); Devdas (2002); Shakti: The Power (2002)
recurring_themes: Indian classical music in large-scale film soundtracks.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction (Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam); R. D. Burman Award (1999)
historical_importance: Composer of Sanjay Leela Bhansali's two landmark musicals of 1999–2002.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for Devdas, with Birju Maharaj, and for Shakti: The Power.
biography: Ismail Darbar is an Indian film composer, instrumentalist, singer and violinist, born in 1964, whose work draws heavily on Indian classical music. He won the R. D. Burman Award in 1999 and the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999). He reunited with Bhansali for Devdas (2002), composing the songs with the Kathak master Birju Maharaj while Monty Sharma wrote the background score. Its songs, including 'Dola Re Dola', won Filmfare Awards for their singers and choreographer. The same year he composed Krishna Vamsi's Shakti: The Power, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a supporting role, with Anu Malik adding a guest composition.

name: Javed Akhtar
career_background: Rose to prominence as half of the screenwriting duo Salim–Javed with Salim Khan, then became a lyricist after the duo split in the early 1980s; father of Farhan and Zoya Akhtar.
debut: Breakthrough as Salim–Javed with Zanjeer (1973).
major_works: Zanjeer (1973); Deewaar (1975); Sholay (1975); Don (1978; 2006 remake); lyrics for Yes Boss, Duplicate, Kal Ho Naa Ho, Veer-Zaara, Swades and Don 2
recurring_themes: The 'angry young man' archetype as a screenwriter; poetic, socially conscious lyrics.
major_awards: 5 National Film Awards; 16 Filmfare Awards, including Best Lyricist for Kal Ho Naa Ho and Veer-Zaara; Padma Shri (1999); Padma Bhushan (2007)
historical_importance: Widely regarded as one of the greatest screenwriters and lyricists in Indian cinema; nominated member of the Rajya Sabha (2010–2016) and a public advocate of secularism and free expression.
relationship_with_actor: Co-wrote Don and Luck by Chance and wrote lyrics for many Khan films from Yes Boss to Dunki, winning Filmfare Awards for Kal Ho Naa Ho and Veer-Zaara.
biography: Javed Akhtar, born on 17 January 1945, is a screenwriter, lyricist, poet and political activist widely regarded as one of the greatest writers in Indian cinema. With Salim Khan he formed the duo Salim–Javed, whose breakthrough Zanjeer (1973) was followed by Deewaar and Sholay (1975), defining the 'angry young man'. After the partnership ended in the early 1980s he became an acclaimed lyricist. He has won five National Film Awards and sixteen Filmfare Awards, received the Padma Shri (1999) and Padma Bhushan (2007), and sat in the Rajya Sabha from 2010 to 2016. His work with Shah Rukh Khan spans both his crafts. His lyrics for Yes Boss (1997) and Duplicate (1998) earned Filmfare nominations. He wrote the lyrics of Chalte Chalte, Kal Ho Naa Ho and Veer-Zaara, winning the Filmfare Award for Best Lyricist for both of the latter, as well as Swades and Love Breakups Zindagi. He is credited as a writer on Don (2006), as author of the 1978 original and the remake, and co-wrote his daughter Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (2009). His lyrics for Don 2 and Dunki (2023) continued the association.

name: K. Subash
career_background: A Tamil director and screenwriter, son of the director R. Krishnan, who trained as an assistant to Mani Ratnam on Nayakan.
debut: Kaliyugam; his second film, Chatriyan, was a blockbuster.
major_works: With Khan: Chennai Express (2013), Dilwale (2015). Wider work: Chatriyan, Pavithra, Abhimanyu, 123.
recurring_themes: Tamil police dramas and action films; later, story work on Hindi comedies.
relationship_with_actor: Two writing credits for Rohit Shetty: the story of Chennai Express, the Tamil Nadu-set action comedy that was one of Khan's biggest hits, and Dilwale, a commercial success.
biography: Krishnan Subash was a Tamil director, the son of R. Krishnan, who learned under Mani Ratnam on Nayakan before making his own debut with Kaliyugam. His second film, the Vijayakanth police drama Chatriyan, was a blockbuster, and he went on to direct Pavithra, Abhimanyu, Ninaivirukkum Varai and 123, while several later projects were shelved. In the 2010s he wrote for Hindi cinema, supplying the story of Rohit Shetty's Chennai Express (2013), in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a Mumbai bachelor stranded in a Tamil village opposite Deepika Padukone, and working on Shetty's Dilwale (2015). When he died on 23 November 2016, press reports identified him as the writer of Chennai Express.

name: Kanika Dhillon
career_background: An Indian novelist, screenwriter and producer who worked as a script supervisor at Red Chillies Entertainment after graduating.
debut: The novel Bombay Duck Is a Fish (2011), launched by Shah Rukh Khan; wide recognition as a screenwriter with Manmarziyaan (2018).
major_works: With Khan: Ra.One (2011), Dunki (2023). Wider work: Manmarziyaan, Kedarnath, Judgementall Hai Kya, Haseen Dillruba, Rashmi Rocket, Raksha Bandhan; Do Patti (2024) as writer and producer.
recurring_themes: Relationship drama and thrillers centred on women.
relationship_with_actor: Began in Khan's company as a script supervisor at Red Chillies, wrote for Ra.One, and later co-wrote Rajkumar Hirani's Dunki. Khan launched her first novel.
biography: Kanika Dhillon worked as a script supervisor at Shah Rukh Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment after graduating and contributed to the writing of Ra.One (2011), Khan's superhero film. Her debut novel, Bombay Duck Is a Fish (2011), was launched by Khan, and she followed it with Shiva and the Rise of the Shadows and The Dance of Durga. Her screenwriting breakthrough came with Manmarziyaan (2018), followed by Kedarnath, Judgementall Hai Kya, Haseen Dillruba, Rashmi Rocket and Raksha Bandhan. She returned to Khan as co-writer of Dunki (2023), Rajkumar Hirani's film about illegal emigration from Punjab. In 2023 she founded Kathha Pictures, whose first production, the Netflix film Do Patti, she also wrote.

name: Ketan Mehta
career_background: Born in Navsari, Gujarat; graduated in film direction from the Film and Television Institute of India and worked as a television producer at the Indian Space Research Organisation.
debut: The Gujarati film Bhavni Bhavai won him acclaim.
major_works: Bhavni Bhavai; Maya Memsaab (1993); Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! (1995); the television serials Captain Vyom and Mr. Yogi
recurring_themes: Comedy, satire, romance, violence and rebellion.
creative_style: Experimental and satirical, shaped by his early freedom to experiment in ISRO television.
major_awards: Maya Memsaab won the National Film Award – Special Mention (Feature Film).
historical_importance: A parallel-cinema filmmaker whose films have screened at Nantes, Moscow and other international festivals.
relationship_with_actor: Cast the young Khan in two unconventional films, both co-starring Mehta's wife Deepa Sahi: the Madame Bovary adaptation Maya Memsaab and the musical parody Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India!
biography: Ketan Mehta was born on 21 July 1952 in Navsari, Gujarat, went to school in Delhi and graduated in film direction from the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune. He then joined the Indian Space Research Organisation as a television producer, where he had almost total freedom to travel across Gujarat and make programmes; he later called the experience vital to his films. His first feature, the Gujarati Bhavni Bhavai, won acclaim, and over his career he has made ten feature films, seven documentaries and the television serials Captain Vyom and Mr. Yogi, ranging across comedy, satire, romance, violence and rebellion. His films have been selected for festivals including Nantes and Moscow. Mehta gave Shah Rukh Khan two early roles far from the romantic-hero mould. In Maya Memsaab (1993), his adaptation of Madame Bovary, Khan plays the young lover of Deepa Sahi's restless wife; the film received a National Film Award – Special Mention. In the musical parody Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! (1995), Khan plays 'Hero', a drifter who foils a don's plan to auction India. Deepa Sahi, Mehta's wife, co-starred in both and co-wrote the second.

name: Maneesh Sharma
career_background: Grew up in Delhi, studied English literature at Hansraj College and filmmaking at the California Institute of the Arts; assistant director at Yash Raj Films on Fanaa, Aaja Nachle and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi.
debut: Band Baaja Baaraat (2010).
major_works: Band Baaja Baaraat (2010); Ladies vs Ricky Bahl (2011); Shuddh Desi Romance (2013); Fan (2016); Tiger 3 (2023)
recurring_themes: Contemporary romance in his early films; stardom and obsession in Fan; spy action in Tiger 3.
creative_style: Grounded, character-focused filmmaking within the Yash Raj Films system.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director (Band Baaja Baaraat)
historical_importance: A Yash Raj Films director who directed a Khan double role and an instalment of the YRF Spy Universe.
relationship_with_actor: Worked as an assistant on Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, directed Khan's double role as a star and his obsessive fan in Fan, and gave him a cameo as Pathaan in Tiger 3.
biography: Maneesh Sharma was born on 6 January 1978 in Delhi, where he attended Delhi Public School, R. K. Puram, and studied English literature at Hansraj College. He trained in filmmaking at the California Institute of the Arts and, after returning to India, worked as an assistant director on Yash Raj Films productions including Fanaa (2006), Aaja Nachle (2007) and Shah Rukh Khan's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi (2008). His debut, Band Baaja Baaraat (2010), with Ranveer Singh and Anushka Sharma, won him the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director; he followed it with Ladies vs Ricky Bahl (2011) and Shuddh Desi Romance (2013). Sharma had conceived Fan in 2006, and Yash Chopra narrated it to Khan that year; the project was revived in late 2013. In the songless thriller (2016) Khan plays both the superstar Aryan Khanna and his obsessive lookalike fan Gaurav, and critics praised the double performance. Sharma's article describes the film as a box-office failure, although it did well overseas. He later directed Tiger 3 (2023), in which Khan appears as Pathaan in a cameo that helps Salman Khan's Tiger escape.

name: Mani Ratnam
career_background: Trained in management and worked as a consultant before entering films.
debut: Pallavi Anu Pallavi (1983, Kannada); breakthrough Mouna Ragam (1986).
major_works: Mouna Ragam (1986); Nayakan (1987); Anjali (1990); Thalapathi (1991); Roja (1992); Bombay (1995); Dil Se.. (1998); Alai Payuthey (2000)
recurring_themes: Love set against political conflict and terrorism.
creative_style: Visually striking, music-led storytelling, often nonlinear.
major_awards: 7 National Film Awards; 4 Filmfare Awards; 7 Filmfare Awards South; Padma Shri (2002)
historical_importance: Regarded as one of the greatest directors in Indian cinema; Nayakan and Anjali were India's Academy Award entries.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan in Dil Se.., the last film of his trilogy with Roja and Bombay, and wrote Saathiya, in which Khan makes a special appearance.
biography: Mani Ratnam, born Gopalaratnam Subramaniam on 2 June 1956, works mainly in Tamil cinema and is regarded as one of the greatest directors in Indian cinema. Although born into a film family, he trained in management and worked as a consultant before entering films with the Kannada Pallavi Anu Pallavi (1983). After early failures he broke through with Mouna Ragam (1986), which won him his first Filmfare Best Director award, and followed it with Nayakan (1987) and Anjali (1990), both India's Academy Award entries, and Thalapathi. He has won seven National Film Awards, four Filmfare Awards and seven Filmfare Awards South, and received the Padma Shri in 2002. With Shah Rukh Khan he made Dil Se.. (1998), set against the insurgency in Assam, the last film of a trilogy with Roja and Bombay. Khan plays a radio journalist who falls for a suicide bomber. The film had an average domestic run but was a major success overseas, became the first Indian film in the UK top ten, won a Netpac Award at the Berlinale, and its A. R. Rahman soundtrack sold six million units. Ratnam later wrote Saathiya (2002), the Hindi remake of his Alai Payuthey, in which Khan appears briefly as an IAS officer.

name: Monty Sharma
career_background: Born in Mumbai; trained from the age of five under his grandfather Pandit Ram Prasad Sharma; nephew of Pyarelal of Laxmikant–Pyarelal; a keyboard player from age sixteen, starting with Mr. India.
major_works: Devdas (2002, score); Silsiilay (2005, score); Black (2005, score); Saawariya (2007, music director); Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013, score); Gadar 2 (2023, score)
recurring_themes: Orchestral background scores, particularly for Sanjay Leela Bhansali.
historical_importance: Background composer for several Bhansali films.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Devdas and Silsiilay, which Khan narrates.
biography: Monty Sharma, born on 17 April 1970 in Mumbai, began learning music at five under his grandfather Pandit Ram Prasad Sharma and is the nephew of Pyarelal of the Laxmikant–Pyarelal duo. At sixteen he became a professional keyboard player with Laxmikant–Pyarelal on Mr. India, and he went on to work with R. D. Burman, Rajesh Roshan, Nadeem–Shravan, Jatin–Lalit and Ismail Darbar. As a background-score composer he is best known for Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Devdas (2002), Black (2005) and Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), and he was music director of Saawariya (2007). He has also judged STAR Voice of India 2. He scored two Shah Rukh Khan films: Devdas and Khalid Mohamed's anthology Silsiilay (2005), which Khan narrates.

name: Mukta Arts
career_background: A Mumbai film company founded by Subhash Ghai: Mukta Films in 1978, reorganised as Mukta Arts in 1982; the first Hindi film producer listed on the stock exchange.
debut: Karz (1980), under Mukta Films.
major_works: With Khan: Trimurti (1995), Pardes (1997). Over 42 productions; also distribution (Mukta Movies), the Mukta A2 multiplex chain and the Whistling Woods International film school.
recurring_themes: Subhash Ghai's large-scale musical melodramas.
historical_importance: A pioneer of corporate structure in Hindi film production.
relationship_with_actor: Two films: Trimurti, a costly multi-starrer with Khan as one of three brothers that lost money, and Ghai's Pardes, a super hit diaspora romance with Khan as the hero.
biography: Mukta Arts is Subhash Ghai's production company. He set up Mukta Films in 1978 and produced Karz with it, then formed Mukta Arts in 1982; it became the first Hindi film producer listed on the stock exchange and has since produced or co-produced over forty films, distributed several hundred more, and opened both the Mukta A2 cinema chain and the Whistling Woods International film school. Its two Shah Rukh Khan films came close together. Trimurti (1995), directed by Mukul S. Anand with Khan, Jackie Shroff and Anil Kapoor as brothers, was expensive and lost money. Pardes (1997), Ghai's own film about an Indian-American marriage arranged across cultures, cast Khan as the adopted son who falls for the bride, and was a super hit.

name: Mukul S. Anand
career_background: A Hindi-film director and producer, nephew of the writer Inder Raj Anand and cousin of Tinnu Anand.
debut: Kanoon Kya Karega (1984), a thriller modelled on Cape Fear.
major_works: With Khan: Trimurti (1995) as director; Army (1996) as producer. Wider work: Sultanat, Insaaf, Agneepath, Hum, Khuda Gawah.
recurring_themes: Large-scale action melodramas, often adapted from Hollywood thrillers.
historical_importance: Director of the Amitabh Bachchan films Agneepath, Hum and Khuda Gawah.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Trimurti, his last completed film, with Khan as one of three brothers, and produced Army, in which Khan has an extended special appearance.
biography: Mukul S. Anand made his debut with Kanoon Kya Karega (1984) and followed it with Aitbaar, a Dial M for Murder variant, and Sultanat (1986), which introduced Juhi Chawla. His first box-office success was Insaaf (1987), and he reached the top rank with Agneepath (1990), which won Amitabh Bachchan a National Award, and then Hum and Khuda Gawah with Bachchan. Trimurti (1995), his last completed film, was a Mukta Arts multi-starrer with Jackie Shroff, Anil Kapoor and Shah Rukh Khan as brothers fighting for their mother. It was expensive and lost money. Anand also produced Army (1996), in which Khan appears in an extended special role. He died on 7 September 1997.

career_background: A producer credited on 2 films in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.

biography: Parvesh C. Mehra is credited as producer on Chamatkar (1992) and Ram Jaane (1995). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Priyadarshan
career_background: Began in Malayalam cinema in the early 1980s and later became known in Bollywood for Hindi adaptations of Malayalam films.
debut: Worked in Malayalam cinema from 1982; entered Hindi cinema with Gardish (1994).
major_works: Chithram (1988); Kilukkam (1991); Kaalapaani (1996); Chandralekha (1997); Hera Pheri (2000); Hungama (2003); Hulchul (2004); Garam Masala (2005); Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007); Billu (2009)
recurring_themes: Comedy of errors and mistaken identity, often adapted from Malayalam originals.
creative_style: Fast ensemble comedy across many genres.
major_awards: 3 National Film Awards; Kerala State Film Awards; Padma Shri (2012)
historical_importance: Has directed over 90 films in several Indian languages.
relationship_with_actor: His Malayalam Chandralekha was remade as Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega, in which Khan makes a special appearance, and he directed Billu, where Khan plays a superstar based on himself.
biography: Priyadarshan, born Priyadarshan Soman Nair on 30 January 1957, has directed over 90 films, mainly in Malayalam and Hindi, and received three National Film Awards, several Kerala State Film Awards and the Padma Shri (2012). He built his reputation in Malayalam cinema with films such as Chithram (1988), Vandanam (1989) and Kilukkam (1991), and continued in the 1990s with Kaalapaani (1996) and Chandralekha (1997). He entered Hindi cinema with the action films Gardish (1994) and Virasat (1997), and in the 2000s became widely known for comedies adapted from Malayalam films, including Hera Pheri, Hungama, Hulchul, Garam Masala and Bhool Bhulaiyaa. His Chandralekha was remade as Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000), with a story credit for Priyadarshan, in which Shah Rukh Khan appears at the end as Rahul Khanna. Priyadarshan directed Khan in Billu (2009), a Red Chillies production remade from the Malayalam Katha Parayumpol, in which Khan plays the superstar Sahir Khan, who returns to a village and publicly honours his forgotten childhood friend, a poor barber played by Irrfan Khan. Variety called the film's climax, Khan's school speech, emotionally effective.

biography: Raaj Kumar Dahima is credited as writer on Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000) and One 2 Ka 4 (2001). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credits alone.

name: Raj Kanwar
career_background: Began by directing plays in Delhi, then worked in Mumbai as an assistant to Shekhar Kapur and Raj Kumar Santoshi.
debut: Directorial debut Deewana (1992), a blockbuster that marked Shah Rukh Khan's screen debut.
major_works: Deewana (1992); Laadla (1994); Jaan (1996); Jeet (1996); Judaai (1997); Daag: The Fire (1999); Badal (2000); Andaaz (2003); Sadiyaan (2010)
recurring_themes: Mainstream romantic and family melodramas; most of his lead characters are named Karan and Kajal.
creative_style: Commercial melodrama with strong song-driven romance.
historical_importance: Launched Shah Rukh Khan's film career with Deewana and cast Lara Dutta and Priyanka Chopra early in theirs in Andaaz.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan's first released film, Deewana, and later gave him a special appearance as Rahul Khanna in Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega.
biography: Raj Kanwar was born on 28 June 1961 and educated at Col. Brown Cambridge School in Dehradun. He began his career directing plays in Delhi before moving to Mumbai, where he assisted Shekhar Kapur and Raj Kumar Santoshi. His directorial debut, Deewana (1992), became a box-office blockbuster and introduced Shah Rukh Khan to film audiences as Raja, the persistent second husband of Divya Bharti's widowed heroine. Kanwar followed it with a string of commercial hits, including Laadla (1994), Jaan (1996), Jeet (1996), Judaai (1997), Daag: The Fire (1999) and Badal (2000), and he cast Lara Dutta and Priyanka Chopra in Andaaz (2003). Most of the lead characters in his films were named Karan and Kajal. His brother was the filmmaker K. Pappu, and his sons Karan Raj Kanwar and Abhay Kanwar have worked as directors and producers. His final film was Sadiyaan (2010). He died of a kidney ailment in Singapore on 3 February 2012. His second film with Khan, Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000), a Salman Khan comedy, used Khan only in a closing special appearance.

name: Rajiv Mehra
career_background: Not documented in the sources consulted; no Wikipedia biography was available.
major_works: Chamatkar (1992); Ram Jaane (1995)
recurring_themes: Both collaborations pair fantasy or crime premises with moral redemption.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan in the ghost comedy Chamatkar and the gangster drama Ram Jaane, both produced by Parvesh C. Mehra.
biography: No standalone biography of Rajiv Mehra was available, so this entry rests on the articles for his two films with Shah Rukh Khan. He directed and co-wrote Chamatkar (1992), a ghost comedy loosely adapted from Blackbeard's Ghost in which Khan plays a naive village graduate helped by the ghost of a gangster, played by Naseeruddin Shah. The Ram Jaane article notes that Chamatkar was an average box-office performer. Mehra reunited with Khan for Ram Jaane (1995), a gangster drama borrowing its premise from Angels with Dirty Faces and the Bengali film Purushottam, in which Khan plays a nameless boy who grows up to be a criminal; it was a hit. Both films were produced by Parvesh C. Mehra.

name: Ram Sampath
career_background: Began composing advertising jingles in Mumbai for brands including Airtel, Docomo, Thums Up and Pepsi; composed pop albums such as Shaan's Tanha Dil (2000); married to the singer Sona Mohapatra.
