relationship_with_actor: Contributed songs to Bhoothnath Returns and composed Raees, whose soundtrack drew over 1.6 billion YouTube streams.
biography: Ram Sampath, born on 25 July 1977, is a composer, music producer and musician who started out writing advertising jingles in Mumbai for brands such as Airtel, Docomo, Thums Up, Pepsi and The Times of India. He moved on to pop albums, including Shaan's Tanha Dil (2000), and then to films such as Khakee, Delhi Belly (2011) and Talaash (2012). He is married to the singer Sona Mohapatra. For Shah Rukh Khan's films he was one of the composers of Bhoothnath Returns (2014) and composed Raees (2017) with JAM8; the Raees article reports that its soundtrack received over 1.6 billion streams on YouTube.

name: Ranjit Barot
career_background: Son of the Kathak dancer Sitara Devi; a drummer, arranger and producer for R. D. Burman, Laxmikant–Pyarelal, Kalyanji–Anandji, Anu Malik and Ismail Darbar, and a longtime associate of A. R. Rahman.
major_works: Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! (1995, songs); Aks (2001, score); Main Hoon Na (2004, score); John McLaughlin's Floating Point (drummer)
creative_style: Percussion-led, drawing on Indian classical, jazz and global drumming traditions.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Background Score (Aks)
historical_importance: Described by John McLaughlin as one of the 'leading edges' in drumming.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! and the background score for Main Hoon Na.
biography: Ranjit Barot, born in 1959 into a family of Indian musicians and dancers, is the son of the Kathak dancer Sitara Devi. He began his career in the 1980s as a drummer, arranger and producer for R. D. Burman, Laxmikant–Pyarelal, Kalyanji–Anandji, U. Srinivas, L. Subramaniam, Anu Malik and Ismail Darbar, and is a longtime associate of A. R. Rahman. Abroad he has performed with John McLaughlin, who has called him one of the 'leading edges' in drumming, and he played on McLaughlin's Grammy-nominated album Floating Point. He won the Filmfare Award for Best Background Score for Aks (2001). For Shah Rukh Khan he composed the songs of Ketan Mehta's musical parody Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! (1995) and the background score of Main Hoon Na (2004).

name: Rohit Shetty
function: Director; producer; stunt director (Rohit Shetty Productions)
career_background: Son of the stuntman M. B. Shetty; began as a stuntman before directing.
debut: Zameen (2003); breakthrough with Golmaal (2006).
major_works: Zameen (2003); Golmaal series (2006–2017); Singham (2011); Bol Bachchan (2012); Chennai Express (2013); Singham Returns (2014); Dilwale (2015); Simmba (2018); Sooryavanshi (2021)
recurring_themes: Action comedy, masala spectacle, car stunts and his 'Cop Universe' franchise.
creative_style: High-energy commercial entertainment with elaborate vehicle stunts.
historical_importance: One of the most commercially successful directors of the 2010s; Chennai Express became the highest-grossing Hindi film at the time.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan's two action comedies, Chennai Express and Dilwale, the second co-produced by Shetty with Red Chillies Entertainment.
biography: Rohit Shetty, born on 14 March 1974 and the son of the stuntman M. B. Shetty, is a director, producer and stuntman whose films mix action comedy with masala spectacle. After his debut thriller Zameen (2003) he broke through with the comedy Golmaal (2006), whose sequels each ranked among the highest-grossing films of their years, and he built the Cop Universe with Singham (2011), Singham Returns (2014), Simmba (2018) and Sooryavanshi (2021). His other hits include All the Best (2009) and Bol Bachchan (2012). He has hosted the stunt show Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi since 2014. With Shah Rukh Khan he made Chennai Express (2013), an action comedy in which Khan's reluctant hero helps a crime boss's daughter escape a forced marriage; it opens with a spoof of the train scene from Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and became, at the time, the highest-grossing Hindi film ever. Shetty then co-produced and directed Dilwale (2015), reuniting Khan and Kajol as lovers torn apart by warring gangster fathers. Critics praised the stars' chemistry but not the screenplay; the film was nonetheless a commercial success.

name: Rumi Jaffery
career_background: A Bhopal-born Hindi-film writer and director, son of the poet Kausar Siddiqui, who has worked in theatre since the age of ten.
debut: Writer on Paayal (1992); directorial debut God Tussi Great Ho (2008).
major_works: With Khan: Anjaam (1994), Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000). Wider work: Coolie No. 1, Hero No. 1, Biwi No.1 (writer, with David Dhawan); Life Partner, Gali Gali Chor Hai, Chehre (director).
recurring_themes: Mainstream comedy, most of it for David Dhawan.
relationship_with_actor: Two writing credits: Rahul Rawail's Anjaam, with Khan as an obsessive stalker, and Raj Kanwar's Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega, in which Khan makes a cameo.
biography: Rumi Jaffery moved from Bhopal to Bombay and debuted as a writer with Paayal (1992). He became known for the comedies he wrote with David Dhawan, including Coolie No. 1, Hero No. 1 and Biwi No.1, and wrote more than fifty scripts before directing God Tussi Great Ho (2008), Life Partner, Gali Gali Chor Hai and Chehre. Early in his writing career he worked on Anjaam (1994), Rahul Rawail's thriller in which Shah Rukh Khan plays an obsessive millionaire who destroys the life of the woman he pursues, played by Madhuri Dixit, and later on Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000), a hit in which Khan makes a cameo. The sources disagree on his birth year (1966 in the infobox, 1974 in the article description), so it is left blank.

name: Sajid Nadiadwala
career_background: Grandson of the producer Abdul Karim Nadiadwala; assistant director to J. P. Dutta on Ghulami before founding Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment at 25.
debut: First production: Zulm Ki Hukumat (1992).
major_works: Jeet (1996); Judwaa (1997); Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000); Mujhse Shaadi Karogi (2004); Heyy Babyy (2007); Housefull (2010); Kick (2014, director); Baaghi (2016)
recurring_themes: Mainstream comedies and action films, often starring Salman Khan or Akshay Kumar.
historical_importance: A prolific commercial producer whose franchises include Housefull and Baaghi; won a debut-director award for Kick.
relationship_with_actor: Produced two films featuring Khan in brief appearances: a closing role in Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega and a song cameo in Heyy Babyy.
biography: Sajid Nadiadwala, born on 18 February 1966, is the grandson of Abdul Karim Nadiadwala, who moved to Mumbai from Nadiad in 1955 and produced hundreds of films. After graduating he worked as an assistant director to J. P. Dutta on Ghulami and as a production assistant in his uncle's company, then founded Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment at 25. His first production was Zulm Ki Hukumat (1992), and he brought Akshay Kumar and Suniel Shetty together in Waqt Hamara Hai (1993). He produced the Salman Khan hits Jeet (1996) and Judwaa (1997), followed by Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000), in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a closing special appearance, and Mujhse Shaadi Karogi (2004). Khan also appears in a song in Sajid Khan's Heyy Babyy (2007), which Nadiadwala produced. His later films include Housefull (2010) and Baaghi (2016), and he won a debutant director award for Kick. His first wife, the actress Divya Bharti, Khan's co-star in Deewana, died in 1993.

name: Sajid–Wajid
career_background: Brothers Sajid Khan and Wajid Khan, sons of the tabla player Sharafat Ali Khan; their maternal grandfather Ustad Faiyyaz Ahmed Khan received the Padma Shri.
major_works: Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002); Kismat Konnection (2008, guest composition)
recurring_themes: Sufi-inflected Bollywood songs.
historical_importance: A leading Bollywood composer duo until Wajid Khan's death on 1 June 2020; Sajid Khan has since worked solo.
relationship_with_actor: Contributed songs to Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam and a guest composition to Kismat Konnection, which Khan narrates.
biography: Sajid–Wajid were the Bollywood composer duo of the brothers Sajid Khan and Wajid Khan, sons of the tabla player Sharafat Ali Khan and grandsons, through their mother, of the Padma Shri recipient Ustad Faiyyaz Ahmed Khan. Active from 1998, they also wrote lyrics and background scores, and Wajid Khan sang some of their songs. Wajid Khan died on 1 June 2020, after which Sajid Khan continued as a solo artist. Their connection to Shah Rukh Khan's films is limited: they were among the composers of Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002) and provided a guest composition for Aziz Mirza's Kismat Konnection (2008), which Khan narrates.

name: Samar Khan
career_background: Not documented in the sources consulted; no Wikipedia biography was available.
major_works: Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005); Shaurya (2008)
relationship_with_actor: Directed two films in which Khan contributes briefly: a cameo as himself in Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye and the voice-over narration of Shaurya.
biography: No standalone biography of the director Samar Khan was available; the Wikipedia article under that name is about a different person. This entry rests on the articles for his two films with Shah Rukh Khan, both of which he directed and co-wrote. Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005), a romantic comedy starring Arshad Warsi and Mahima Chaudhry whose title comes from a Cadbury advertising tagline, features Khan as himself in a cameo. Shaurya (2008), a military courtroom drama produced by Moser Baer and based on the play Court Martial and the film A Few Good Men, features Khan's voice-over narration and was praised for the performances of Kay Kay Menon and Javed Jaffrey.

name: Shibani Bathija
career_background: An Indian screenwriter who studied English at DePauw University and communications at San Francisco State, then worked in advertising with Sony.
debut: Fanaa (2006) and Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006).
major_works: With Khan: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006), My Name Is Khan (2010). Wider work: Fanaa, Kidnap.
recurring_themes: Romantic and social drama for Karan Johar and Yash Raj Films.
major_awards: Filmfare nomination for Best Screenplay for Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, shared with Karan Johar.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote both of Khan's films with Karan Johar in this period: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, a drama about adultery between two unhappily married people, and My Name Is Khan, in which Khan plays a man with Asperger syndrome in post-9/11 America; the latter was a financial success.
biography: Shibani Bathija moved from advertising into film after showing a script to Karan Johar, who passed it to Yash Raj Films. In 2006 she wrote two major releases: Kunal Kohli's Fanaa and Johar's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna. The latter cast Shah Rukh Khan as a bitter former footballer who falls for another man's wife, played by Rani Mukerji, and earned her a Filmfare Best Screenplay nomination with Johar. She then wrote Kidnap (2008) and Johar's My Name Is Khan (2010), in which Khan plays Rizwan, an autistic Muslim man who sets out to meet the American president after his stepson is killed in a hate crime. The film was a financial success, especially overseas.

name: Shridhar Raghavan
career_background: An Indian screenwriter, brother of the director Sriram Raghavan, who became the principal screenwriter of the Yash Raj Spy Universe.
debut: Credits from 2000; National Award-winning screenplay for Apaharan (2005).
major_works: With Khan: Pathaan (2023), Tiger 3 (2023). Wider work: Apaharan, War (2019), War 2 (2025), Alpha (2026).
recurring_themes: Espionage action thrillers.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Screenplay for Apaharan.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the two 2023 Spy Universe films in which Khan appears as Pathaan: the lead role in Pathaan, which marked his commercial comeback, and a cameo in Tiger 3.
biography: Shridhar Raghavan won the National Film Award for Best Screenplay for Apaharan (2005) and later became the main writer of Yash Raj Films' Spy Universe, scripting War (2019), Pathaan (2023), Tiger 3 (2023), War 2 (2025) and Alpha (2026). Pathaan, directed by Siddharth Anand, cast Shah Rukh Khan as an exiled Indian agent and was his first lead release in more than four years; it was a major commercial comeback. Raghavan wrote Khan into Maneesh Sharma's Tiger 3 the same year, where Pathaan appears in a cameo alongside Salman Khan's Tiger. He is the brother of Sriram Raghavan, the director of Johnny Gaddaar and Andhadhun.

biography: Subhash Ghai, born on 24 January 1945, was one of the most prominent Hindi filmmakers of the 1980s and 1990s, known for iconic characters, grand sets, dramatic climaxes and themes of divine justice and duty. His films include Kalicharan (1976), Karz (1980), Hero (1983), Karma (1986), Ram Lakhan (1989), Khalnayak (1993) and Taal (1999). He directed Dilip Kumar in Vidhaata, Karma and Saudagar, and won his only Filmfare Award for Best Director for Saudagar (1991). In 1982 he founded Mukta Arts, which went public in 2000; in 2006 he received the National Film Award for Best Film on Other Social Issues for producing Iqbal and founded the Mumbai film school Whistling Woods International. He received the IIFA Award for Outstanding Contribution to Indian Cinema in 2015. With Shah Rukh Khan he first worked as producer of the action drama Trimurti (1995), Mukta Arts' first production, directed by Mukul S. Anand. He then wrote, produced and directed the musical romance Pardes (1997), in which Khan plays a loyal foster son who protects his brother's fiancée, played by the newcomer Mahima Chaudhry. Pardes was one of the first major Bollywood successes in the United States and won Ghai the Filmfare Award for Best Screenplay.

biography: Uttam Singh, born on 25 May 1948 in Punjab, is a music director and well-known violinist who has also worked as a music arranger, programmer and recordist on many Bollywood films. He assisted Ilaiyaraaja on numerous Tamil films before establishing himself as a composer, working in Bollywood, semi-classical, classical and Punjabi folk styles. His best-known score is for Yash Chopra's Dil To Pagal Hai (1997), the romantic musical starring Shah Rukh Khan, Madhuri Dixit and Karisma Kapoor, with lyrics by Anand Bakshi. It won him the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director, one of the film's eight Filmfare wins. He was also among the several composers credited on Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002).

biography: UTV Motion Pictures was the feature-film unit of UTV Software Communications, founded in 1996 by Ronnie Screwvala and Zarina Screwvala. It became one of India's leading film studios and one of the largest production studios in South Asia, with activities across development, production, marketing, distribution, licensing, merchandising and syndication. It partnered with Hollywood studios including 20th Century Studios, Walt Disney Pictures and Sony Pictures, distributed Disney's films in India, and operated as Disney UTV in 2012–2013. In July 2017, shortly after Jagga Jasoos, it stopped Hindi film production. With Shah Rukh Khan, UTV co-produced Ashutosh Gowariker's Swades (2004), which failed commercially but became a cult classic. It also produced and distributed Rohit Shetty's Chennai Express (2013) with Red Chillies Entertainment; Screwvala and Siddharth Roy Kapur are among its credited producers, and it became the highest-grossing Bollywood film at the time.

biography: Vanraj Bhatia (31 May 1927 – 7 May 2021) was an Indian composer best known for his work in Indian New Wave cinema and one of the country's leading composers of Western classical music. He won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for the television film Tamas (1988), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Creative and Experimental Music (1989) and the Padma Shri (2012). He also wrote background scores for mainstream films, including two for Shah Rukh Khan: the ghost comedy Chamatkar (1992), whose songs were by Anu Malik, and Subhash Ghai's Pardes (1997), whose songs were by Nadeem–Shravan. He died in Mumbai in May 2021.

biography: Viveck Vaswani, credited in the films as Vivek Vaswani, started as an actor in Khandaan, India's first television soap opera, then produced the Marathi film Kis Bai Kiss, the serial Nai Dishayen and the film Gawaahi. At Sippy Films he co-produced Patthar Ke Phool, Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman and Aatish with G. P. Sippy, playing small roles in them as well. His article credits him with launching Raveena Tandon and Shah Rukh Khan, and records that he gave Khan a place to stay when he first came to Bombay. Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), which Vaswani co-produced, cast Khan as a small-town engineer trying to make it in the city and was a commercial success. He later produced Dulha Mil Gaya (2010) and wrote its story; Khan has an extended special appearance in it. He became dean of Pearl Academy and joined the Indian National Congress in 2024.

biography: Zoya Akhtar, born on 14 October 1972 to Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani, completed a filmmaking diploma at New York University and assisted Mira Nair, Tony Gerber and Dev Benegal before becoming a writer and director. Her debut, Luck by Chance (2009), a satire of the Hindi film industry produced by her brother Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment, won her the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director and wide critical acclaim. More than a dozen stars play themselves in it, including Shah Rukh Khan, who warns Farhan Akhtar's rising actor about fame and urges him to stay close to his old friends. She broke through commercially with Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011), which won her the Filmfare Award for Best Director, and won the award again for Gully Boy (2019). In between she directed Dil Dhadakne Do (2015) and a segment of Bombay Talkies (2013), the anthology celebrating a century of Indian cinema whose closing song features Khan among many stars. She co-founded Tiger Baby Films with Reema Kagti in 2015 and has made the series Made in Heaven and Dahaad.

biography: Aamir Khan made his first screen appearance as a child in Yaadon Ki Baaraat (1973), directed by his uncle Nasir Hussain, and became a leading man with Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988). Through the 1990s he and Shah Rukh Khan, together with Salman Khan, defined Hindi film stardom, and from Lagaan (2001) onward he built a reputation for socially themed blockbusters, among them Taare Zameen Par, 3 Idiots, PK and Dangal, while producing through Aamir Khan Productions. Their only collaboration in this filmography is Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), Aamir's adaptation of Forrest Gump, in which Shah Rukh Khan appears briefly as himself; Aamir starred in and co-produced the film, which was a commercial disaster. He has won nine Filmfare Awards and four National Film Awards.

biography: Aanand L. Rai is a director and producer known for the romantic comedy-dramas Tanu Weds Manu (2011) and Tanu Weds Manu Returns (2015) and the romantic drama Raanjhanaa (2013), the last two of which earned him Filmfare nominations for Best Director. He then directed the big-budget romantic drama Zero (2018), produced by his Colour Yellow Productions with Red Chillies Entertainment, followed by Atrangi Re (2021) and Raksha Bandhan (2022). In Zero, Shah Rukh Khan plays Bauua Singh, a brash man with dwarfism from Meerut who abandons a scientist with cerebral palsy (Anushka Sharma), is drawn into a film star's world (Katrina Kaif), and tries to redeem himself by volunteering for a mission to Mars. Critics praised the visual effects and the performances but found the second half overwrought, and the film was highly unsuccessful at the box office. Rai's article heads this period 'Career decline (2018–present)'.

biography: Abhijat Joshi grew up in an academic family in Ahmedabad, began in Gujarati school theatre, and has taught English at Otterbein University in Ohio since 2003. His play about the 1992 Gujarat riots, A Shaft of Sunlight, brought him to Vidhu Vinod Chopra, for whom he wrote Kareeb and Mission Kashmir, and he became Rajkumar Hirani's regular co-writer on Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006), 3 Idiots (2009), PK (2014) and Sanju (2018). His only Shah Rukh Khan film is Dunki (2023), Hirani's comedy-drama about the 'donkey route' of illegal emigration, in which Khan plays a former soldier who helps a group of friends from a Punjab village try to reach London.

His only connection to Shah Rukh Khan is The Zoya Factor (2019), adapted from Anuja Chauhan's novel about a woman considered a lucky charm by the Indian cricket team, in which Khan is the narrator. The film was a box-office disaster.

biography: Abrar Alvi wrote three of the most admired films in Hindi cinema for Guru Dutt — Pyaasa (1957), Kaagaz Ke Phool (1959) and Sahib Bibi Aur Ghulam (1962), which he also directed. Pyaasa is on Time magazine's All-Time 100 Movies list. He started in college theatre in Nagpur and in later decades wrote for mainstream films, including Rajesh Khanna's Janta Hawaldar and Begunaah. His one Shah Rukh Khan credit comes near the end of his career: Guddu (1995), a family melodrama directed by Prem Lalwani in which Khan plays the title role. Alvi died on 18 November 2009.

The company has no article under its own name; Adlabs became Reliance MediaWorks, the Reliance Group's film and entertainment services business, which offers processing, digital intermediate, visual effects, 2D-to-3D conversion, studio rental and post-production and runs operations in India, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its television arm, BIG Synergy, produced Kaun Banega Crorepati and Indian Idol. Linking the 2019 credit to this corporate history rests on the article name change, so confidence is low.

biography: Adnan Sami was raised and educated in the United Kingdom, the son of a Pakistani Air Force veteran and diplomat, and built a reputation as a virtuoso pianist; Keyboard magazine called him the fastest keyboard player in the world. He became a popular singer and composer in Hindi music and was naturalised as an Indian citizen in 2016, later receiving the Padma Shri. His only Shah Rukh Khan credit is Shaurya (2008), Samar Khan's drama about the court martial of a soldier, for which he composed the songs; Khan's involvement is limited to narration.

His second film, Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), adapted Forrest Gump with Aamir Khan in the lead; Shah Rukh Khan makes a brief appearance as himself, and the film failed commercially. Chandan's next film was Loveyapa (2025), starring Junaid Khan and Khushi Kapoor.

biography: Ajay–Atul are the brothers Ajay and Atul Gogavale, who began with the devotional album Vishwa Vinayak, combining Ganpati mantras with symphonic music, and became the leading composers of Marathi cinema with Natarang and Sairat. In Hindi their work includes Agneepath (2012) and Dhadak, and they have a National Film Award and four Filmfare Awards Marathi. Their one Shah Rukh Khan film is Zero (2018), Aanand L. Rai's romance in which Khan plays Bauua Singh, a man of short stature; it was one of the biggest failures of his career.

Before film he worked in consumer goods and founded Colosceum Media, which produced television formats such as MTV Roadies, MTV Splitsvilla and MasterChef India. He is credited as a producer on Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), Viacom18's co-production with Aamir Khan Productions and Paramount Pictures, in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a brief appearance as himself. He is credited as a writer on Tubelight (2017), Kabir Khan's war-era fable starring Salman Khan, which adapts Little Boy, and in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a cameo as a magician. biography: Amol Palekar, born on 24 November 1944, is an actor, director and producer in Hindi and Marathi cinema, as well as a painter and author. He was part of the movement that popularised 'middle cinema', with popular films including Chhoti Si Baat (1975), Chitchor (1976), Bhumika (1977), Baaton Baaton Mein (1979) and Gol Maal (1979), and he won three Filmfare Awards and six Maharashtra State Film Awards as Best Actor. He directed Paheli (2005), produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment and based on Vijayadan Detha's Rajasthani short story 'Duvidha', with a screenplay by his wife Sandhya Gokhale. Shah Rukh Khan plays both Kishanlal, a merchant's son who leaves his bride on their wedding night, and the ghost who takes his form and wins her love. The film opened the Zimbabwe International Film Festival, screened at Sundance, and was India's official submission to the Academy Awards; Taran Adarsh called it one of the finest films of recent times.

He came to Hindi cinema with Dum Laga Ke Haisha (2015) for Yash Raj Films, and the following year wrote the background score for Fan (2016), Maneesh Sharma's thriller in which Shah Rukh Khan plays both the film star Aryan Khanna and Gaurav, a young fan from Delhi who looks like him.

biography: Arun 'Atlee' Kumar, born on 21 September 1986, is a filmmaker working primarily in Tamil cinema. His debut, Raja Rani (2013), won him the Vijay Award for Best Debut Director and the Tamil Nadu State Award for best dialogue, and he followed it with three hits starring Vijay: Theri (2016), Mersal (2017) and Bigil (2019), which Shah Rukh Khan described as 'Chak De India on steroids'. His films have also attracted plagiarism allegations. Atlee made his Hindi debut with Jawan (2023), produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment. Khan plays Azad, a prison jailer who leads a band of women inmates in heists exposing corruption, and his father Vikram, a soldier framed by an arms dealer. The film broke opening-day records, overtook Pathaan as the highest net-grossing Hindi film in India, and won Khan the National Film Award for Best Actor. Critics credited Khan's screen image with selling its conceit, although some found the story chaotic.

Shah Rukh Khan appears in its opening section as Mohan Bhargav, a scientist who guards a fragment of the Brahmāstra. The film was a hit and one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of its year.

industry: Assamese cinema and music; Hindi cinema
career_background: An Assamese singer, songwriter, filmmaker and politician whose songs on communal amity and justice are widely popular in Assam, West Bengal and Bangladesh.

biography: Bhupen Hazarika wrote and sang mainly in Assamese, and his songs on humanity and brotherhood made him one of the most loved cultural figures in eastern India. He is credited with introducing Assamese and North-East folk music to Hindi cinema at the national level, won the National Award for music direction in 1975 and received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1992. He composed the songs for Gaja Gamini (2000), the painter M. F. Husain's film about Madhuri Dixit as an eternal muse, in which Shah Rukh Khan appears as himself. Hazarika died on 5 November 2011.

biography: Bhushan Kumar became head of T-Series in 1997, after the murder of his father Gulshan Kumar, running it with his uncle Krishan Kumar. Under him the music label became a major film producer, with releases such as Aashiqui 2 and Nautanki Saala in 2013, and he began developing Mogul, a biopic of his father. He is credited as a producer on Bhoothnath Returns (2014), Nitesh Tiwari's political comedy starring Amitabh Bachchan as a ghost, in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a cameo; the film was profitable.

He led the Kathak Kendra in New Delhi for many years, opened his own school, Kalashram, after retiring in 1998, and received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986. In Devdas (2002), Sanjay Leela Bhansali's lavish adaptation starring Shah Rukh Khan, Aishwarya Rai and Madhuri Dixit, he is credited with a song composition alongside the film's main composers. The film was a commercial success. He died on 17 January 2022.

It became known for small-town romances and comedies such as Raanjhanaa and Shubh Mangal Zyada Saavdhan, and also backed the horror film Tumbbad. Zero (2018), co-produced with Gauri Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment, cast Shah Rukh Khan as Bauua Singh opposite Anushka Sharma and Katrina Kaif. Her best-known role is Maya in Maya Memsaab (1993), Ketan Mehta's adaptation of Madame Bovary, in which an explicit scene with the young Shah Rukh Khan caused controversy. She is married to Mehta and co-wrote his next film, Oh Darling! Yeh Hai India! (1995), a surreal political satire set over one night in Bombay, with Khan in the lead. She directed Tere Mere Phere in 2011.

She co-wrote Jab Tak Hai Jaan (2012), the last film directed by Yash Chopra, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays Samar, an army bomb-disposal expert who makes a vow to God for the life of the woman he loves (Katrina Kaif) and later meets a young filmmaker (Anushka Sharma). The film was a hit.

Lucky Oye!; both won National Film Awards. He then made Love Sex Aur Dhokha, Shanghai and Detective Byomkesh Bakshy!. For Bombay Talkies (2013), the centenary anthology produced with Karan Johar, Zoya Akhtar and Anurag Kashyap, he directed a segment adapted from a Satyajit Ray story; Shah Rukh Khan appears in the film as himself.

biography: Gauri Shinde, born on 6 July 1974, grew up in Pune and graduated from the Symbiosis Institute of Mass Communication. She interned with the documentary director Siddharth Kak and worked in advertising at agencies including Lowe Lintas, where R. Balki, whom she married in 2007, was creative director. She made over 100 advertising films and short films; her short Oh Man! (2001) was selected for the Berlin Film Festival. Her feature debut, English Vinglish (2012), inspired by her mother and marking Sridevi's comeback, premiered at Toronto and was a critical and commercial success, winning her the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director. She wrote and directed Dear Zindagi (2016), co-produced by her Hope Productions with Red Chillies Entertainment and Dharma Productions. Alia Bhatt plays Kaira, a young cinematographer, and Shah Rukh Khan plays Dr. Jehangir 'Jug' Khan, the free-spirited psychologist who helps her confront her fear of abandonment and gently declines her romantic feelings. The film was a commercial success, and reviewers praised the chemistry between its two leads.

biography: Gautam Rajadhyaksha studied chemistry at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, joined Lintas in 1974 and became one of the country's most sought-after portrait photographers after a 1980 shoot with Shabana Azmi, Tina Munim and Jackie Shroff. He also wrote two screenplays for Rahul Rawail: Bekhudi (1992), which introduced Kajol, and Anjaam (1994), a thriller in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a rich man whose fixation on a married flight attendant (Madhuri Dixit) leads to murder and revenge. He died on 13 September 2011.

He co-wrote Fan (2016), Maneesh Sharma's thriller about Gaurav Chandna, a Delhi youth obsessed with the film star Aryan Khanna; Shah Rukh Khan played both roles, with heavy prosthetics for the fan.

career_background: One of the most popular and successful actresses of mainstream Hindi cinema, promoted as the 'Dream Girl', and a BJP member of the Lok Sabha for Mathura since 2014.

historical_importance: A leading Hindi-film heroine of the 1970s.

biography: Hema Malini was one of the biggest female stars of 1970s Hindi cinema, winning the Filmfare Award for Best Actress for her double role in Seeta Aur Geeta (1972) and starring in Sholay and Dream Girl, often opposite Dharmendra, whom she married in 1980. She made her directing debut with Dil Aashna Hai (1992), which she also produced and co-wrote; Shah Rukh Khan, then at the start of his film career, plays Karan opposite Divya Bharti as a dancer searching for her birth mother. She has represented Mathura in the Lok Sabha since 2014.

career_background: A Lucknow-born Hindi-film writer and producer who did theatre at Kirori Mal College, wrote for NDTV and television serials such as Kkusum and Bhootwala, and is married to the writer Kanika Dhillon.

biography: Himanshu Sharma moved from television writing in Delhi and Mumbai into film with Strangers (2007) and became Aanand L. Rai's regular writer, scripting Tanu Weds Manu (2011), Raanjhanaa (2013) and Tanu Weds Manu Returns (2015), the last of which won him National Awards. He wrote Zero (2018), Rai's big-budget romance with Shah Rukh Khan as a short, brash man from Meerut who falls for a scientist with cerebral palsy (Anushka Sharma) and an alcoholic film star (Katrina Kaif). It was one of the most notable failures of Khan's career.

biography: Honey Irani acted as a child in the 1950s and 1960s and met Javed Akhtar on the set of Seeta Aur Geeta; they married in 1972 and their children are Zoya and Farhan Akhtar. After the marriage ended she turned to writing and co-wrote Yash Chopra's Lamhe and Darr (1993). In Darr, Shah Rukh Khan plays Rahul, a student whose obsession with Kiran (Juhi Chawla) drives him to stalk and threaten her and her fiancé; the role, with Chawla's name stammered as 'K-k-k-Kiran', became one of his most famous. She later wrote Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai and the Krrish films for Rakesh Roshan.

biography: Hriday Lani worked across the parallel and commercial cinema of the 1970s to 1990s, writing for Gaman, Mirch Masala and Salaam Bombay! as well as for Shalimar, Agni Sakshi and Yeshwant, and shared the Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue for Sarfarosh (1999). He co-wrote Maya Memsaab (1993), Ketan Mehta's Hindi reworking of Madame Bovary with Deepa Sahi as a restless doctor's wife, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays Lalit, one of her lovers.

name: Hridaynath Mangeshkar
career_background: A composer and occasional singer, the only son of Deenanath Mangeshkar and the younger brother of Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle, known in the industry as Balasaheb.
debut: The Marathi film Akash Ganga (1955).
major_works: With Khan: Maya Memsaab (1993). Wider work: Jait Re Jait, Umbartha, Nivdung (Marathi); Subah, Lekin..., Maya Memsaab (Hindi).
recurring_themes: Complex, poetry-based compositions that demand singers of great range.
major_awards: Filmfare Marathi Lifetime Achievement Award; V. Shantaram Lifetime Achievement Award.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Ketan Mehta's Maya Memsaab, for which he composed the songs; Khan has a supporting role.
biography: Hridaynath Mangeshkar began composing with the Marathi film Akash Ganga in 1955 and has worked selectively since, mainly in Marathi cinema, with a small number of Hindi scores, of which Lekin... and Maya Memsaab are the best known. His songs, often settings of poetry, are known for difficult metres written for singers such as his sisters Lata and Asha. Maya Memsaab (1993), Ketan Mehta's adaptation of Madame Bovary, was one of Shah Rukh Khan's earliest films; Khan plays a young man who becomes involved with the heroine.

biography: Hussain Dalal writes dialogue for Hindi films and also acts. His credits include Ayan Mukerji's Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani (2013), 2 States (2014), Margarita with a Straw and Karwaan, and he returned to Mukerji for Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022), in which Shah Rukh Khan appears in the opening section as the scientist Mohan Bhargav. In 2017 he was one of the mentors on The Great Indian Laughter Challenge.

name: Ilaiyaraaja
career_background: A composer, arranger, conductor, multi-instrumentalist and singer, known as 'Isaignani' and 'Maestro', who has composed over 6,500 songs and scored nearly 1,500 films in nine languages, mainly Tamil.
debut: Annakili (1976).
major_works: With Khan: Hey Ram (2000). Wider work: Mouna Ragam, Nayakan, Thalapathi; in Hindi, Sadma, Cheeni Kum, Paa.
recurring_themes: Fusion of Indian folk and classical music with Western classical harmony and string writing.
historical_importance: Voted the country's greatest film composer in a 2013 CNN-IBN poll; one of the first Indian film composers to use Western classical harmony.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Kamal Haasan's Hey Ram, for which he wrote songs and score; Khan has a supporting role.
biography: Ilaiyaraaja, born Gnanathesigan, transformed Tamil film music from the late 1970s by fusing folk and Carnatic idioms with Western classical harmony and orchestration, and by 2025 had composed for nearly 1,500 films. He was given the title 'Maestro' by the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra in London and in 1986 recorded the first computer-assisted Indian film soundtrack, for Vikram. He composed the songs and score of Hey Ram (2000), Kamal Haasan's bilingual drama about Partition and the assassination of Gandhi, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays the archaeologist Amjad Khan, the hero's friend.

name: Imtiaz Ali
debut: Socha Na Tha (2005).
major_works: Socha Na Tha (2005); Jab We Met (2007); Love Aaj Kal (2009); Rockstar (2011); Highway (2014); Tamasha (2015); Jab Harry Met Sejal (2017); Amar Singh Chamkila (2024); Main Vaapas Aaunga (2026)
recurring_themes: Romance, restlessness, travel and self-discovery.
creative_style: Road-movie romances centred on characters seeking themselves.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue; several Filmfare Best Director nominations
historical_importance: One of the defining romance filmmakers of 2000s–2010s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote and directed Jab Harry Met Sejal, casting Khan as a lonely Punjabi tour guide in Europe opposite Anushka Sharma; Ali later called it a missed opportunity.
biography: Imtiaz Ali, born on 16 June 1971, is a filmmaker best known for writing and directing the romantic comedies Socha Na Tha (2005), Jab We Met (2007) and Love Aaj Kal (2009), and the dramas Rockstar (2011), Highway (2014) and Tamasha (2015); his later work includes Amar Singh Chamkila (2024) and Main Vaapas Aaunga (2026). His films have earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue and several Best Director nominations. His article marks Jab Harry Met Sejal (2017) as the start of a commercial decline. In that film Shah Rukh Khan plays Harry, a womanising, homesick tour guide in Europe who reluctantly helps a Gujarati tourist (Anushka Sharma) search for her lost engagement ring and falls in love with her. The film was shot across Prague, Amsterdam, Vienna, Lisbon and Budapest and did well overseas, but received mixed-to-negative reviews. Anupama Chopra argued that Ali could not fit Khan's chaste romantic persona to his own 'more bruised brand of romance'. Ali later rated the film 3 out of 10 and called it a missed opportunity.

name: Jaideep Sahni

relationship_with_actor: Wrote Chak De! India, the sports drama in which Khan plays Kabir Khan, disgraced former hockey captain turned coach of the women's national team, loosely based on Maharaj Krishan Kaushik. It was a blockbuster and a career landmark for Khan.
biography: Jaideep Sahni began writing lyrics in jam sessions with Palash Sen and screenplays after reading the published script of Gandhi. Ram Gopal Varma produced his first two films, Jungle and Company; the latter won seven Filmfare Awards, including his Best Story and Best Dialogue. He then wrote Khosla Ka Ghosla and a string of Yash Raj films, including Bunty Aur Babli, Rocket Singh and Shuddh Desi Romance. His most important film is Chak De! India (2007), directed by Shimit Amin, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a hockey player branded a traitor after a lost match against Pakistan who returns to coach the women's team to a world title. The film was a blockbuster and is one of Khan's most admired performances.

After 1920 London, its first major soundtrack credit was Raees (2017), where its composition 'Zaalima', picturised on Shah Rukh Khan and Mahira Khan, was a big hit; Raees was a moderate success at the box office. JAM8 has since composed for Raabta, Race 3 and other Hindi, Telugu and Bengali films.

She later became CEO of Jio Studios, which is credited on Khan's Dunki (2023), and President of Media and Content Business at Reliance Industries.

It is credited as a producer on I See You (2006), a romantic comedy starring Arjun Rampal, in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a self appearance.

name: K. C. Bokadia
career_background: A Rajasthan-born Hindi-film producer and director from Merta City, described by the Deccan Chronicle as 'the fastest producer to make 50 films', with more than 60 films by 2021.
debut: As producer, Rivaaj (1972); as director, Aaj Ka Arjun (1990).
major_works: With Khan: Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002). Wider work: Pyar Jhukta Nahin, Teri Meherbaniyan, Naseeb Apna Apna, Main Tera Dushman; directed Phool Bane Angaaray, Police Aur Mujrim.
recurring_themes: Mass melodrama, including films built around animals.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam, which he produced; Khan plays the lead, a jealous husband.
biography: K. C. Bokadia began producing with Rivaaj (1972) and made dozens of mainstream films over five decades, among them Pyar Jhukta Nahin, Naseeb Apna Apna and the dog-led Teri Meherbaniyan, and directed Aaj Ka Arjun with Amitabh Bachchan. He produced Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002), K. S. Adhiyaman's long-delayed remake of the Tamil film Thaikulame Thaikulame, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a husband whose jealousy over his wife's childhood friend (Salman Khan) breaks up their marriage.

name: K. S. Adhiyaman
industry: Tamil cinema; Hindi and Telugu cinema
career_background: A Tamil director, screenwriter and lyricist who apprenticed under K. Vijayan for eight films and wrote dialogue for Suresh Menon before directing.
debut: Thoorathu Sondham (1992); first success Thotta Chinungi (1995).

biography: K. S. Adhiyaman made his name in Tamil cinema with Thotta Chinungi (1995), a relationship drama about a husband's suspicion of his wife, after an unnoticed debut and dialogue work for Suresh Menon. In early 1998 he began remaking it in Hindi as Aap Mere Hai Sanam with Shah Rukh Khan, Madhuri Dixit and Salman Khan; it was eventually released in 2002 as Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam. Khan plays Gopal, whose jealousy of his wife's closeness to her childhood friend breaks up the marriage. Adhiyaman later started Mujhse Shaadi Karogi in 2002, a project that went to another director.

biography: Kabir Khan studied at Kirori Mal College and Jamia Millia Islamia and worked in documentary before his first feature, Kabul Express (2006). He became known for Ek Tha Tiger (2012) and Bajrangi Bhaijaan (2015), both starring Salman Khan, and reunited with the star for Tubelight (2017), a war-era fable adapted from Alejandro Monteverde's Little Boy, which he wrote, directed and co-produced. Shah Rukh Khan makes a cameo as a magician. Sources disagree on Kabir Khan's birth year (1971 in the infobox, 1968 in the description), so it is left blank.

It co-produced Saathiya (2002), Shaad Ali's Hindi remake of Mani Ratnam's Alaipayuthey with Vivek Oberoi and Rani Mukerji, in which Shah Rukh Khan has a cameo. The film was a commercial success.

name: Kamal Haasan
function: Director; producer; screenwriter; actor (Raaj Kamal Films International)
career_background: Actor, filmmaker and politician who has made over 230 films in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Hindi, Kannada and Bengali; founded the party Makkal Needhi Maiam in 2018 and joined the Rajya Sabha in 2025.
major_works: Hey Ram (2000)
recurring_themes: In Hey Ram, communal violence, Partition and the assassination of Gandhi.

major_awards: Padma Shri (1990); Padma Bhushan (2014); Chevalier of the Order of Arts and Letters (2016); Filmfare Award South for Best Actor – Tamil (Hey Ram); invited to join the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (2025)
historical_importance: One of the most prolific figures in Indian cinema; Hey Ram was India's submission for the Academy Awards.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote, produced, directed and starred in Hey Ram, casting Khan as his secular Pathan friend Amjad in Khan's Tamil debut; Khan's Dreamz Unlimited distributed the Hindi version.
biography: Kamal Haasan, born on 7 November 1954, is an actor, filmmaker and politician who works mainly in Tamil cinema and has made over 230 films in six languages as actor, director, producer, screenwriter, playback singer and lyricist. He received the Padma Shri in 1990, the Padma Bhushan in 2014 and France's Order of Arts and Letters in 2016, and was invited to join the Academy's actors' branch in 2025. He was the first Tamil actor to turn his fan clubs into welfare associations, launched the party Makkal Needhi Maiam in 2018 and became a member of the Rajya Sabha in July 2025. Haasan wrote, produced, directed and starred in Hey Ram (2000), an alternate-history drama about Partition and the assassination of Gandhi, made simultaneously in Tamil and Hindi. Shah Rukh Khan plays Amjad Ali Khan, a Pathan archaeologist and the hero's closest friend, who dies at the hands of a mob while trying to turn him from hatred. It was Khan's Tamil-language debut, and his Dreamz Unlimited distributed the Hindi version. The film won three National Film Awards and was India's Academy Award submission, but it failed commercially.

name: Kamna Chandra
career_background: A writer of radio plays for All India Radio and of film stories and dialogue, from Muzaffarnagar; mother of the novelist Vikram Chandra, the critic Anupama Chopra and the director Tanuja Chandra.
major_works: With Khan: Gaja Gamini (2000). Wider work: Prem Rog, Chandni, 1942: A Love Story; the television show Kashish.
recurring_themes: Romantic melodrama.
relationship_with_actor: One film: M. F. Husain's Gaja Gamini, which she co-wrote, in which Khan appears as himself.
biography: Kamna Chandra wrote plays for All India Radio before writing stories and dialogue for Hindi films, among them Prem Rog, Chandni and 1942: A Love Story, the last directed by her son-in-law Vidhu Vinod Chopra. Her children include Vikram Chandra, Anupama Chopra and Tanuja Chandra. She co-wrote Gaja Gamini (2000), M. F. Husain's film about an idealised woman across the ages, played by Madhuri Dixit, in which Shah Rukh Khan appears as himself. It failed at the box office.

name: Karan Razdan
career_background: A Kashmiri Pandit actor, writer and director who began in television, writing and acting in Rajani and directing the detective serial Tehkikaat.
debut: Television: Rajani (1980s); Tehkikaat as producer-director.
major_works: With Khan: Trimurti (1995). Wider work: Dilwale, Diljale, Deewane (writer); Girlfriend, Hawas, Souten: The Other Woman, Umar, Mittal v/s Mittal (writer-director).
recurring_themes: Action-romance screenplays in the 1990s; controversial themes as director.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Mukul S. Anand's Trimurti, which he co-wrote; Khan is one of three brothers in the ensemble lead.
biography: Karan Razdan began on television, writing and acting in Rajani and creating the detective serial Tehkikaat with Vijay Anand. In 1990s cinema he wrote action romances such as Dilwale, Diljale and Deewane, and he later directed films including Girlfriend (2004), Hawas, Souten: The Other Woman and Umar. He co-wrote Trimurti (1995), Mukul S. Anand's multi-starrer with Jackie Shroff, Anil Kapoor and Shah Rukh Khan as brothers, which lost money despite its scale.

name: Karim Morani
career_background: A Hindi-film producer who co-owns the production and event-management company Cineyug with his brother Ali Morani.

major_works: With Khan: Chennai Express (2013); also, per his article, co-producer of Ra.One. Wider work: Arjun, Vardi, Yodha, Damini, Raja Hindustani.

relationship_with_actor: Co-produced Chennai Express with Khan's Red Chillies, and his article says he also co-produced Ra.One. Khan attended the funeral of Morani's mother in 2015, which shows a personal friendship as well.
biography: Karim Morani entered film production with Rahul Rawail's Arjun (1985) and followed it with Vardi, Yodha, Damini and Dushmani, most of them starring Sunny Deol, before producing Aamir Khan's Raja Hindustani (1996). With his brother Ali he runs Cineyug, which also manages events. After a long break from production he teamed up with Shah Rukh Khan. He is credited on Chennai Express (2013), Rohit Shetty's action comedy, one of Khan's highest-grossing films, and his article also credits him on Ra.One, though the roster here does not list him on that film. The roster follows the film credits.

biography: Khalid Mohamed spent nearly three decades as a critic and editor, at The Times of India, Filmfare, DNA and the Hindustan Times, and wrote three screenplays for Shyam Benegal, including Zubeidaa (2001), based on the life of his mother, Zubeida Begum. As director he made three films: Fiza, Tehzeeb and Silsiilay (2005), a three-part film about women in relationships with Bipasha Basu, Tabu and Celina Jaitly, which Shah Rukh Khan narrates. He has also made documentaries and staged the play Kennedy Bridge.

name: Kiran Rao

biography: Kiran Rao started as an assistant director on Lagaan and worked in Aamir Khan's production company, whose films she later co-produced; she was married to Khan until 2021. She directed Dhobi Ghat (2011) and Laapataa Ladies (2024), which India later submitted to the Academy Awards. She is credited as a producer on Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), the Forrest Gump remake in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a brief appearance as himself. The film was a commercial disaster.

biography: Salur Koteswara Rao, known as Koti, grew up in the household of the composer S. Rajeswara Rao and formed the duo Raj–Koti with T. V. Raju's son Somaraju in the early 1980s; they scored about 180 films before splitting in 1994. Koti then worked solo on over 350 films. In Hindi he wrote the background score for Trimurti (1995), Mukul S. Anand's Subhash Ghai-produced epic with Jackie Shroff, Anil Kapoor and Shah Rukh Khan.

biography: Krishan Kumar Dua is the younger brother of Gulshan Kumar, who founded Super Cassettes Industries (T-Series), and with his nephew Bhushan Kumar he has run the company since Gulshan Kumar's murder in 1997. As an actor he is best known for Bewafa Sanam (1995). He is credited as a producer on Bhoothnath Returns (2014), Nitesh Tiwari's political comedy with Amitabh Bachchan, in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a cameo. The film was profitable.

biography: Krishna Vamsi trained under Ram Gopal Varma and debuted with Gulabi (1995). Ninne Pelladata and Sindhooram, both National Award winners in Telugu, followed, and then Antahpuram (1998), a drama about a woman trying to escape a feudal family with her son. His only Hindi film, Shakti: The Power (2002), remade Antahpuram with Karisma Kapoor, Nana Patekar and Shah Rukh Khan in a supporting role as a rough-mannered man who helps the heroine. It was a flop.

biography: Kundan Shah (19 October 1947 – 7 October 2017) was a director and writer best known for the comedy classic Jaane Bhi Do Yaaro (1983), which won the National Film Award for Best Debut Film of a Director, and for the television series Nukkad (1986–1987), made with Saeed Akhtar Mirza. With Saeed and Aziz Mirza he co-founded the production company Iskra in 1985. Shah directed Shah Rukh Khan in Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa (1994), a coming-of-age comedy in which Khan plays Sunil, a happy-go-lucky musician who schemes to win his bandmate Anna and finally helps her marry the man she loves. The film won Shah the Filmfare Award for Best Film (Critics) and Khan the award for Best Actor (Critics). It is widely considered one of Khan's best performances, and Khan has said it is his favourite film. A retrospective in The Indian Express noted that a conventional version would have made Sunil the villain of Chris and Anna's love story, whereas Shah made him the hero.

major_works: With Khan: Dulha Mil Gaya (2010), solo. As Jatin–Lalit with Khan: Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Yes Boss, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Mohabbatein, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham.

biography: Lalit Pandit and his brother Jatin, as Jatin–Lalit, wrote some of the best-known Hindi film music of the 1990s and early 2000s, including the soundtracks of Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, all starring Shah Rukh Khan. They come from a musical family from Haryana; Pandit Jasraj was their uncle and the actresses Sulakshana and Vijayta Pandit are their sisters. After the duo stopped working together in 2006, Lalit composed alone, including songs and score for Dulha Mil Gaya (2010), a flop in which Khan has an extended special appearance.

name: Laxmikant–Pyarelal
career_background: An Indian composing duo of Laxmikant Shantaram Kudalkar (1937–1998) and Pyarelal Ramprasad Sharma (born 1940), known as L-P, who composed for about 750 films between 1963 and 1998.
debut: Parasmani (1963).
major_works: With Khan: Trimurti (1995). Wider work: Dosti, Bobby, Amar Akbar Anthony, Karz, Hero, Ram Lakhan, Khalnayak.
recurring_themes: Mainstream melody across every commercial genre.
historical_importance: The most prolific composing unit in Hindi film history.
relationship_with_actor: One late credit: the songs of Trimurti, one of the last films they scored before Laxmikant's death in 1998.
biography: Laxmikant–Pyarelal were the dominant composers of mainstream Hindi cinema from the mid-1960s to the late 1980s, scoring around 750 films for nearly every major banner. Laxmikant, who grew up poor and learned the mandolin as a boy, and Pyarelal, a violinist, began together on Parasmani (1963). Their association with Shah Rukh Khan is limited to Trimurti (1995), produced by Subhash Ghai, for whom they scored Hero, Ram Lakhan and Khalnayak. Laxmikant died in 1998.

name: Louis Banks
career_background: A composer, keyboardist, record producer and singer born in Calcutta to Nepali parents and raised in Darjeeling, often called the 'Godfather of Indian jazz'; his great-grandfather composed the former Nepalese national anthem.
major_works: With Khan: Duplicate (1998). Wider work: jazz fusion recordings; advertising jingles; film scores.
recurring_themes: Jazz and fusion.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Mahesh Bhatt's Duplicate, for which he wrote the background score; Khan plays a double role. The film failed.
biography: Louis Banks was born Dambar Bahadur Budaprithi; his father, a trumpeter who played in a European band in Calcutta as George Banks, renamed him after Louis Armstrong when he took up guitar and trumpet at thirteen. He became the leading figure of Indian jazz and a prolific composer for advertising and film. For Shah Rukh Khan he wrote the background score of Duplicate (1998), Mahesh Bhatt's comedy in which Khan plays both a timid chef and a lookalike gangster. The film was a commercial failure.

name: M. F. Husain
career_background: A painter of narrative works in a modified Cubist style, a founding member of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group, whose later nude depictions of Hindu deities and Bharat Mata led to lawsuits and self-exile.
debut: As filmmaker, the documentary Through the Eyes of a Painter (1967).
major_works: With Khan: Gaja Gamini (2000). Wider work: the paintings Voices and series on Gandhi, Mother Teresa, the Ramayana and the Mahabharata; the film Meenaxi: A Tale of Three Cities.
recurring_themes: Indian myth, modern history and the female muse.
historical_importance: One of the central figures of Indian modernist painting.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Gaja Gamini, his first Hindi feature, which he wrote and directed as a tribute to Madhuri Dixit; Khan appears as himself. It failed commercially.
biography: M. F. Husain was the best-known Indian painter of the twentieth century, a founder of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group whose Cubist-influenced narrative canvases took on Gandhi, the epics and modern Indian life. His painting Voices sold for $2.5 million in 2020. He wrote and directed Gaja Gamini (2000), a film structured as a meditation on a single woman across centuries, played by Madhuri Dixit, his muse; Shah Rukh Khan makes a self appearance. The film failed commercially. Husain left India after legal cases over his later work and died in London on 9 June 2011.

Keeravani has composed mainly for Telugu cinema since 1990, from Kshana Kshanam and Annamayya to the Baahubali films and RRR, whose song 'Naatu Naatu' won the Academy Award and the Golden Globe. In Hindi, where he is credited as M. M. Kreem, his work includes Zakhm, Jism and Paheli (2005), Amol Palekar's Rajasthani folk tale produced by Red Chillies, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays both a neglectful merchant and the ghost who falls in love with his bride. Paheli was average in India, a hit overseas, and India's submission to the Academy Awards.

name: Madan Mohan
career_background: A Hindi-film composer of the 1950s–1970s, born in Baghdad and raised in Chakwal and Lahore, remembered above all for his film ghazals with Lata Mangeshkar, Mohammed Rafi and Talat Mahmood.
major_works: With Khan: Veer-Zaara (2004), posthumous. Wider work: Adalat, Anpadh, Woh Kaun Thi?, Haqeeqat, Dastak, Heer Raanjha.
recurring_themes: Ghazal-based film songs.

relationship_with_actor: Credited posthumously on Yash Chopra's Veer-Zaara: the soundtrack was built from his unused tunes, revised by his son Sanjeev Kohli. Khan plays an Indian Air Force pilot who falls for a Pakistani woman; the film was a commercial success.
biography: Madan Mohan Kohli was born in Baghdad, where his father worked for the Iraqi police, and grew up in Chakwal and Lahore before going to Bombay. He became known for the ghazals he wrote for films such as Adalat, Anpadh and Woh Kaun Thi?, mostly for Lata Mangeshkar, and died in 1975. Nearly three decades later Yash Chopra used his unused compositions, revised by his son Sanjeev Kohli, as the soundtrack of Veer-Zaara (2004), the cross-border romance starring Shah Rukh Khan and Preity Zinta. The credits say 'original compositions'.

biography: Madras Talkies is the company Mani Ratnam set up with his brother G. Srinivasan in 1995, after earlier producing with Aalayam Productions; its first film was Iruvar (1997). It co-produced Dil Se.. (1998), the last part of Ratnam's trilogy on politics and love after Roja and Bombay, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays Amarkant, a radio reporter who becomes obsessed with a mysterious woman from Assam (Manisha Koirala). Its 'Chaiyya Chaiyya' sequence on top of a moving train became one of the most famous song sequences in Hindi film.

He has directed five films, one of which is Shahrukh Bola "Khoobsurat Hai Tu" (2010), a low-budget film about a woman told by Shah Rukh Khan that she is beautiful, with Khan appearing as himself. biography: Manohar Shyam Joshi wrote Hum Log (1984), India's first television soap opera, and Buniyaad (1987), a Partition saga, and was also an experimental novelist who won the Sahitya Akademi Award for Kyap. He wrote the Hindi dialogue for Hey Ram (2000), Kamal Haasan's bilingual film about Partition and the assassination of Gandhi, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays the archaeologist Amjad Khan. Joshi died in New Delhi on 30 March 2006; Prime Minister Manmohan Singh called him one of the most influential Hindi writers of recent times.

biography: Mansoor Khan, born on 30 May 1958, is the son of the filmmaker Nasir Hussain and the cousin of Aamir Khan, whom he cast in several films. He studied at IIT Bombay, Cornell University and MIT before entering Hindi cinema. His debut, Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), was a major hit that won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and his only Filmfare Award for Best Director, and it revived the musical romance in Hindi cinema. He followed it with Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikander (1992). His last two films as director, Akele Hum Akele Tum (1995) and Josh (2000), were moderately successful. Josh, which he directed and co-wrote for Venus Films, drew on West Side Story for a tale of rival gangs in 1980 Goa. Shah Rukh Khan plays Max Dias, leader of the local Eagles, who fiercely guards his twin sister (Aishwarya Rai) against the rival gang leader's brother. Critics praised its music and performances but found the script weak. Khan returned in 2008 as co-producer, with Aamir Khan, of Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na, and now lives in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, where he farms.

biography: Nikkhil Advani, born Nikhil Suresh Advani on 28 April 1971 in Bombay, is a director, producer and screenwriter who co-founded the company Emmay Entertainment with his sister Monisha Advani and Madhu Bhojwani. He studied chemistry at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and started his career assisting Saeed and Aziz Mirza on the television series Naya Nukkad (1994), then co-wrote Iss Raat Ki Subah Nahin (1996). He was an assistant director to Karan Johar on Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998), in which he also appeared in the Neelam talk-show sequence, and on Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001), and to Aditya Chopra on Mohabbatein (2000), all starring Shah Rukh Khan. Advani made his directorial debut with Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), written by Johar and set in New York. Khan plays Aman, a cheerful neighbour secretly dying of a heart condition, who steers the woman he loves towards her best friend. The film was critically acclaimed, became the highest-grossing Hindi film of the year worldwide, and won two National Film Awards and eight Filmfare Awards.

biography: Rajkumar 'Raju' Hirani, born on 20 November 1962, began as a film editor and advertising filmmaker; his first feature as a professional editor was Vidhu Vinod Chopra's Mission Kashmir (2000). His directorial debut, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003), was a critical and commercial success that won the Filmfare Award for Best Film (Critics) and brought Hirani the Filmfare Award for Best Screenplay. Its sequel Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006) was the second-highest grosser of its year, and both won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film. His coming-of-age comedy 3 Idiots (2009) became the highest-grossing Indian film of its time, and he followed it with the religious satire PK (2014). His films are known for treating serious social issues with humour and have won four National Film Awards and eleven Filmfare Awards. Hirani co-wrote, co-produced, edited and directed Dunki (2023) with Jio Studios and Red Chillies Entertainment. Shah Rukh Khan plays Hardy, an ex-soldier who leads villagers from Punjab to England on the illegal 'donkey flight' route and returns 25 years later to bring home the dying woman he loves. The film received mixed reviews but was one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of 2023.

biography: Ramesh Sippy, born on 23 January 1947, is a director, actor and producer best known for directing Sholay (1975), often regarded as one of the most influential films made in India. In 2017 he founded the Ramesh Sippy Academy of Cinema & Entertainment in Mumbai. He directed Shah Rukh Khan in Zamaana Deewana (1995), a masala film produced by G. P. Sippy under the Sippy Films banner. Khan plays Rahul, whose gang-leader father is feuding with his former friend; police-hired psychologists steer Rahul towards his father's enemy's daughter, played by Raveena Tandon, to end the feud. Sippy's wife, Kiran Juneja, plays one of the psychologists. The film under-performed at the box office.

biography: Sanjay Leela Bhansali, born on 24 February 1963, is a filmmaker and composer known for his aesthetics and musical vision, particularly in period dramas. His honours include seven National Film Awards, thirteen Filmfare Awards, a BAFTA nomination and the Padma Shri (2015). After his debut, Khamoshi: The Musical (1996), he achieved critical and commercial success with the romantic dramas Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999) and Devdas (2002). He won the National Film Award for Best Hindi Film for Black (2005); after the failures of Saawariya and Guzaarish he returned with Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), Bajirao Mastani (2015) and Padmaavat (2018). Devdas, his version of Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel, cast Shah Rukh Khan as the London-educated heir who abandons his childhood love Paro (Aishwarya Rai), turns to drink, finds refuge with the courtesan Chandramukhi (Madhuri Dixit) and dies at Paro's gates. Built on sets costing ₹200 million and premiered at Cannes, it was the highest-grossing Indian film of the year and India's Academy Award submission. It won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and swept the major Filmfare awards, including Best Actor for Khan, although Indian reviews of the lead performances were divided.

biography: Santosh Sivan, born on 8 February 1964, is a cinematographer, director, producer and actor working in Malayalam, Tamil and Hindi cinema. A graduate of the Film and Television Institute of India, he has completed 55 feature films and 50 documentaries and is regarded as one of India's finest cinematographers. His honours include twelve National Film Awards, six Filmfare Awards and the Pierre Angénieux Excellens in Cinematography, and his directorial work Halo won the National Film Award for Best Children's Film. His cinematography for Mani Ratnam's Dil Se.. (1998), starring Shah Rukh Khan, won both the National Film Award and the Filmfare Award. He then directed and co-wrote Aśoka (2001), an epic about the early life of the Mauryan emperor, produced by Khan and Juhi Chawla's Dreamz Unlimited. Khan plays the prince who, travelling in disguise, marries a fugitive princess, becomes a brutal conqueror, and renounces violence after the Kalinga war. The film was acclaimed internationally, with Peter Bradshaw calling it 'a big, brash and deeply enjoyable Bollywood epic', and Sivan won Filmfare and IIFA awards for its cinematography.

biography: Shimit Amin was born in 1975 in Kampala, Uganda, and grew up in Florida, where he graduated in mathematics from the University of Florida. He helped organise North Florida's first Asian and Asian American film festival in 1991, then worked on industrial and independent projects in Miami and California. He came to Indian cinema as editor of Bhoot (2003) and made his first film as director, the police thriller Ab Tak Chhappan (2004), a box-office success. His next film, Chak De! India (2007), written by Jaideep Sahni and produced by Aditya Chopra for Yash Raj Films, starred Shah Rukh Khan as Kabir Khan, a Muslim former hockey captain branded a traitor after a loss to Pakistan, who redeems himself by coaching the neglected women's national team to a World Cup. It was a critical and commercial success, winning the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and five Filmfare Awards, including Best Actor for Khan. Amin's third film was Rocket Singh: Salesman of the Year (2009) with Ranbir Kapoor.

major_awards: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in English (Land Gold Women), as producer.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote and directed I See You, starring Arjun Rampal, in which Khan appears as himself.
biography: Vivek Agrawal left a master's programme to work as a production assistant and directed one film, I See You (2006), a romantic comedy starring Arjun Rampal in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a self appearance. He went on to run Phantom Films, producing Queen, Udta Punjab and Super 30, and supervised the first season of Netflix's Sacred Games.

name: Vivek Lalwani
career_background: A producer credited on one film in this filmography, with no Wikipedia article of their own.
major_works: With Khan: Guddu (1995).
relationship_with_actor: One film with Khan, credited as producer: Guddu (1995), directed by Prem Lalwani, with Khan in the lead as Guddu Bahadur.
biography: Vivek Lalwani is credited as producer on Guddu (1995). No Wikipedia article or other independent biography was located; this row is built from the film credit alone.

name: Vivek Sharma
career_background: A Jabalpur-born filmmaker with an M.Sc. in physics who assisted Mahesh Bhatt for six years and then joined Shah Rukh Khan and Juhi Chawla's company Dreamz Unlimited.
debut: Bhoothnath (2008).
major_works: With Khan: Bhoothnath (2008). As assistant: Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke, Chaahat, Duplicate; worked at Dreamz Unlimited on Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, Aśoka, Chalte Chalte.
relationship_with_actor: Close to Khan before directing: he assisted Mahesh Bhatt on Chaahat and Duplicate and then worked at Khan's Dreamz Unlimited. His debut, Bhoothnath, gave Khan an extended special appearance as the boy's father; it was a semi-hit.
biography: Vivek Sharma moved to Mumbai in 1992 and spent six years assisting Mahesh Bhatt, including on Shah Rukh Khan's Chaahat and Duplicate. He became close to Khan and Juhi Chawla and joined their company Dreamz Unlimited, working on Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani, Aśoka and Chalte Chalte. His directorial debut, Bhoothnath (2008), starred Amitabh Bachchan as a ghost befriended by a boy; Khan plays the boy's father in an extended special appearance. The film was a semi-hit.

name: Yo Yo Honey Singh
career_background: A Delhi-born singer, music producer and actor, born Hirdesh Singh, who began as a hip-hop producer in 2003 and became one of the highest-paid music artists in Hindi films by 2012.
debut: 'Glassy' with Ashok Masti (2006); album International Villager.
major_works: With Khan: Bhoothnath Returns (2014). Wider work: Cocktail, Chennai Express ('Lungi Dance'), Yaariyan.
recurring_themes: Punjabi hip-hop and party songs.
relationship_with_actor: One film: Bhoothnath Returns, for which he composed a song; Khan has a cameo. He had also produced 'Lungi Dance', the tribute song in Khan's Chennai Express.
biography: Yo Yo Honey Singh worked in the underground Punjabi music scene before International Villager made him a star, and by 2012 he was reportedly receiving record fees for Hindi film songs. He composed 'Lungi Dance', the Rajinikanth tribute added to Shah Rukh Khan's Chennai Express (2013), and is credited as a song composer on Bhoothnath Returns (2014), in which Khan makes a cameo.

name: Zayed Khan
career_background: A former Hindi-film actor and producer, son of Sanjay Khan, who studied business at Montgomery College and film at the London Film Academy.
debut: Chura Liyaa Hai Tumne (2003).
major_works: With Khan: Love Breakups Zindagi (2011), as producer. As actor: Main Hoon Na, Shabd, Dus, Yuvvraaj, Blue, Anjaana Anjaani.
relationship_with_actor: Co-produced Love Breakups Zindagi through Born Free Entertainment with Dia Mirza and Sahil Sangha; Khan appears as himself. Zayed had played Khan's half-brother in Main Hoon Na (2004).
biography: Zayed Khan made his debut in 2003 and is best remembered as Lucky, the rebellious college student who turns out to be Shah Rukh Khan's half-brother, in Farah Khan's Main Hoon Na (2004). He moved into production in 2011 with Born Free Entertainment, co-owned with Dia Mirza and Sahil Sangha, whose first film, Love Breakups Zindagi, starred him and Mirza and included a self appearance by Shah Rukh Khan.
